**batch 3:** XOM comparative-label collision fixed — when a CIK's dataset lacks the original filing, comparative columns inherit the later filing's `fy` and duplicate selector options; `xbrl._dedupe_period_labels` now enforces unique (fy, fp) labels at extraction (earlier end walks its year back; **batch 7 (2026-09-29):** bank revenue composite — JPM seeded with 2013–2014 quarters because banks file quarterly revenue as `NoninterestIncome` + `InterestIncomeExpenseNet` while the generic `Revenues` chain holds only annual facts (JPM's quarterly `Revenues` stops in 2014; WFC's in 2020; GS files none), and revenue is the canonical anchor so *every* joined metric (net income, EPS) was pinned a decade stale; finance SICs (6000–6299) now use a composite revenue series summing both components (verified exact match to quarterly `Revenues` on BAC 2026 Q1/Q2, diff 0); JPM/WFC re-seeded with current quarters; **batch 8 (2026-09-29):** finance `Revenues` preference — MET (insurer, SIC 6331) seeded with $0.7B revenue because the generic chain prefers the `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` tag, which for insurers is a fee-income sub-component, while the filer's own `Revenues` ($19B total) sat later in the chain; finance SICs (6000–6999) now prefer quarterly `Revenues` when absolutely current (≤180 days from today since batch 9's threshold change — a *relative* check can't work since JPM files nothing else quarterly in the chain), with the bank composite as fallback for stale/missing `Revenues`. **batch 9 (2026-09-29):** REIT net-income tag abandonment — Realty Income (O) stopped filing quarterly `NetIncomeLoss` after 2025-Q3 (last quarterly fact 273 days behind the replacement tag), so net income showed `None` for 2026 Q1/Q2 while EPS was present; the `NET_INCOME` chain now falls back to `NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic` then `ProfitLoss`, and the tag-abandonment staleness threshold tightened 400→180 days (two filing cycles — the relative rule compares same-filer tags, so slow filers are never penalized); O re-seeded with ni=$311.8M/$344.0M. **batch 9 (2026-09-29):** LLY missing `Liabilities` tag — Eli Lilly never files a standalone `Liabilities` tag (only `LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity` + `StockholdersEquity`), so Total Liabilities showed "—" in the balance-sheet tab and compare table; missing instants are now derived from the accounting identity (Assets − Equity, same filing, only where both components exist; explicit filings never overwritten) — verified 108.4B = 142.3 − 33.9 on live LLY. **batch 10 (2026-09-29):** instant-fact staleness blind spot — `_newest_in_window` ignored facts without a `start`, so the 180-day tag-abandonment rule never engaged for balance-sheet metrics and the first chain tag always won even when abandoned years ago; UNH showed Total Equity "—" for all 8 quarters (`StockholdersEquity` abandoned 2015, fresh `…IncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest` ignored) and PG showed Cash & Equivalents "—" for all 8 quarters (`CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue` abandoned 2019); a `None` window now counts facts of any duration, and both metrics render (PG identity holds exactly: 72.2+54.3=126.5). **batch 10 (2026-09-29):** GS Q2 2026 basic EPS blank — the 10-Q filed only `EarningsPerShareDiluted`; per-quarter fallback now fills missing basic-EPS ends from diluted (basic still preferred where present; differs by fractions of a percent) — Q2 2026 now $20.98 live. **batch 11 (2026-09-29):** LLY CapEx tag discovery — Eli Lilly never filed `PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment` and abandoned `PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets` in 2022; it files "Capital expenditures" as `PaymentsToAcquireOtherPropertyPlantAndEquipment`, so FCF showed "—" for all 8 quarters; the CAPEX chain now includes that tag (freshness rule picks it; NVDA precedent) — LLY FCF now $0.16B–$7.76B across quarters, Overview card renders $7.76B. **batch 11 (2026-09-29):** 52/53-week 9M window — Costco's 36-week 9M YTD cash-flow fact is 251 days, below the old 255-day floor (the Q4-derivation path used 250), so COST's Q3 FCF could not be uncumulated and showed "—"; both 9M windows unified at a 240-day floor — Q3 FY2026 FCF now $2.04B, all 8 quarters present. **batch 11 (2026-09-29):** missing-equity identity derivation — `_derive_missing_liabilities` generalized to `_derive_missing_balance_sheet`: filers with no standalone equity tag (Visa files only Assets + Liabilities) now get Total Equity = Assets − Liabilities (V: $35.66B); assets is never derived; explicitly filed values never overwritten — AMD/WMT/AMZN re-seeded and their liabilities now derive too ($17.24B/$195.68B/$544.07B). Fresh tickers AMZN + CAT seeded clean (CAT all metrics present; AMZN liabilities derived, FCF −$8.8B honest). **batch 12 (2026-09-30):** Q4 EPS derivation fixed — per-share values were un-cumulated by subtraction (FY_EPS − 9M_EPS) even though the two figures divide by different share counts; DUOL's FY2025 Q4 rendered diluted $0.94 *above* basic $0.88 (arithmetically impossible). `_derive_q4_income` now derives Q4 EPS as Q4 net income over the implied Q4 share count ((12·FY_avg − 9·9M_avg)/3 from the filed NI/EPS pairs), falling back to precision-rounded subtraction when NI facts are missing/zero — DUOL now $0.90 basic > $0.89 diluted; residual sub-cent flips from filing-rounded inputs (UBER FY2024 Q4) documented as a limitation. **batch 12 (2026-09-30):** FCF suppressed for all finance SICs (6000–6999) — SoFi files a CapEx tag so it rendered a misleading −$3.99B FCF while every bank/insurer/REIT peer shows "—"; OpCF for lenders is dominated by balance-sheet flows, so the metric is not meaningful. Fresh tickers SOFI + DUOL + UBER + RBLX seeded clean. **Data-source limits (not defects):** Visa files no EPS tags at all in companyfacts (per-share-class EPS uses dimensional facts, which companyfacts excludes) — EPS shows "—" by design; REIT/bank/insurer FCF stays "—" (no CapEx-line filing / not a meaningful metric) — banks (BAC/JPM/WFC), MET, O, XOM single-filing YTD gaps **Environmental caveat:** SEC Archives document fetches currently 403 ("Undeclared Automated Tool") while index listings + JSON API work — discovery finds the right exhibits but downloads are blocked; enrichment is best-effort and self-heals on future refreshes. **Data-source limits (not defects):** Visa files no EPS tags at all in companyfacts (per-share-class EPS uses dimensional facts, which companyfacts excludes) — EPS shows "—" by design

## Phase roadmap (reference)

- **Phase 0:** Setup + EDGAR exploration (weeks 0–1)
- **Phase 1:** Data flowing for one company (weeks 1–4)
- **Phase 2:** Single-company browsing UI (weeks 5–8)
- **Phase 3:** Scale to all US public companies + watchlist + downloads (weeks 9–14)
- **Phase 4:** Earnings calendar + alerts (weeks 15–18)
- **Phase 5:** AI analysis (weeks 19–24)
- **Phase 6:** News feed (weeks 25–28)

Each phase has explicit "done" criteria — don't jump ahead.
| 2026-10-06 | Batch 18 (8-K disclosure integration audit — 5 defects fixed): the 8-K guidance/transcript feature shipped 2026-10-05 but rendered "Not available for this period" for most tickers — audit against real data (NVDA/TSLA/JPM/AAPL/MSFT) found and fixed five defects. (1) **fix** stale-ticker backfill gap — `enrich_company` only runs on first fetch, so tickers fetched before 2026-10-05 never got disclosures; `get_detail` now lazily backfills missing press-release highlights/guidance/transcript (best-effort, never raises, commits only on its own session; short-circuits + disk-cached SEC responses keep repeat visits cheap). (2) **fix** 8-K matching window — `_match_8k` anchored on the 10-Q/10-K *filing* date with a 21-day window, systematically missing annual periods (JPM's 10-K filed 31 days after its earnings 8-K) and borderline 10-Qs (23-day gap); now anchors on the period end (first Item 2.02 8-K within 60 days after report date, nearest the formal filing). JPM matches went 2/4 → 4/4. ## Batch 97 (2026-10-19) — partial-highlight forensic sweep: 60 → 12

**Forensics:** classified 134 residual quarters across the 60 partial companies — 59 no-period (discovery never returned the quarter), 40 discovery-gap (8-K found, no release doc), 28 extract-gap (doc found, extraction failed), 7 no-8k.

**Discovery fixes (`services/ir_download.py`):**
- 10 new exhibit-naming conventions in `_pick_release_doc` (ACN bare `8-kexhibit`, AFRM `shareholderlett` truncation, CART `sha/shar` + ordinal-word guard, CCI month+year+`release`, CTVA reversed-quarter `4q` + `schedules` supplement penalty, DAL `announces`+month, EQIX loose `pr`+junk with date/quarter guard, GPC truncated `earn`+quarter, MKC bare `reports`, UNH `991`-leading-letter tier 0).
- **Paginated submissions:** `EdgarClient.submissions_bucket()` + `_merge_filings_recent()` — `discover_earnings_filings` now pages `filings.files` buckets until it has n_quarters 10-Q/10-K (BAC's recent bucket held only 3 10-Q + 1 10-K — the 59 no-period quarters). Bucket JSON top-level IS the recent-shaped block.
- **Tier-0 99.2/99.3 exclusion:** 99.2+ supplements (BAC `ex993`, MET `ex992`) never outrank the 99.1 release; undotted `ex9901` (CDNS) still matches via `(?!\d|\.\d)` guard (allows `.htm` dot, blocks `.2`/`.3`).
- **`_lone_exhibit_fallback`:** single-exhibit 8-Ks led by 2.02 (TSLA `exhibit.htm`, PNC `a2025_11x07xbaabxvf.htm`, HAL `livemastererdocument.htm`, UNP `ex_713315.htm`) — guard is "2.02 first item", not "exactly 2.02" (most earnings 8-Ks carry 9.01).
- **`_match_8k` guards:** candidates must be filed ≥7d after period end (TSLA's 2-day deliveries 8-K, REGN's 6-day no-exhibit 8-K) and ≤ the 10-Q/10-K filing date (PNC's post-10-Q conference 8-K, FDX's recast-supplement 8-K); nearest to filing date wins. Fixed 3 wrong-content quarters (PNC×2 conference decks, FDX recast supplement) — cleared and re-filled.
- **`oldest_period_end` + 8-K pagination:** discovery extends past n_quarters to cover the oldest stored period (V's 2024-06-30 was the 9th filing — stored window lagged submissions via EDGAR companyfacts delay) and pages until 8-Ks reach the oldest period's window (MS's Oct-2024 8-K sat in an older bucket than its Nov-2024 10-Q).

**Extraction fixes (`data/filings.py`):** bare `EX-99` admin line (NEE), `Page X of Y` (MET), date lines (LLY), `For release: Immediately` variant; financial-table guard rejects table-shaped "Highlights" sections (LLY, WM); highlights heading tightened to start-or-end (WM footnote verb); lede table-fragment drop (MET) + footnote skip (WM); `_skip_contact_block` index bug.

**Results:** 48 quarters rescued (60→12 partial, 192→~228 at 8/8). Honest Nones by design: EOG (supplement-only ex-99.1), AFRM (image-only letter), LIN (5-line stub), SKYD (never files 2.02). Out-of-scope findings: XOM mapped to wrong CIK (SEC ticker map points to holdings entity — seeding defect); SHOP is a 6-K foreign filer (no 10-Q for 2024-09-30); GS cover-page layout needs a title-block-skip heuristic.

**Tests:** 31 new (26 discovery/extraction + 5 matcher/pagination). Full suite 829 green, `git diff --check` clean.

### Batch 102 — financial bullets win over business "Highlights" sections (2026-10-20)
Halliburton's releases open with financial bullets ("Net income of $0.64 per diluted share") right after the headline, then carry a later "Selective Technology & Highlights" section of business-PR bullets (product launches, partnerships). The extractor used to return the first "Highlights" heading match, burying the figures. `_extract_highlights_section` now collects ALL candidates (leading bullet block + every "Highlights" section) and picks the one densest with reported financial figures (≥2 figure lines, ≥40% of lines financial); ties keep the earliest — the pre-batch-102 behavior when nothing is financial. `_leading_bullet_block` handles wrapped bullet continuations (HAL Q2 2025's "... free cash flow1 of / approximately $582 million."), stopping at the dateline paragraph (item closed + non-bullet next line). Live backfill: HAL 8/8 quarters now lead with financial bullets (Q2 2025 rescued from business-only by the wrap fix).

**Tests:** 6 new (financial priority, wrapped bullets, threshold, fallbacks). Full suite 871 green, `git diff --check` clean. Live: /company/HAL, /detail, /tearsheet, / all 200; detail renders the rescued financial bullets.

### Batch 103 — 6-K earnings-release discovery for foreign filers (2026-10-20)
Closes the carried "SHOP 6-K discovery" follow-up. SHOP's Q3-2024 quarter (2024-09-30) was the DB's last 6-K gap: its quarterly filing sits beyond the submissions feed's recent window (no paginated buckets), but the earnings release IS in the feed as a 6-K (`form6kq32024pressrelease.htm`, acc. 0001594805-24-000089). Three changes in `services/ir_download.py`: (1) `_extract_sec_filings` also promotes earnings-looking 6-Ks to period anchors — the primary-doc name must carry a quarter token for the 6-K's own reportDate quarter AND the reportDate must be that quarter's month-end (AGM/code-of-conduct/BFCM 6-Ks carry no quarter token; event-dated dividend 6-Ks are not month-ends). (2) `_extract_6ks` feeds every 6-K into the non-2.02 fallback pool (their `items` field is empty, so they can never enter the 2.02 pool). (3) `_match_8k_non202_fallback`: the 6-K's primary doc (the cover form, routinely press-release-named) is excluded from the exhibit pick — the real release was the oddly-named `a3pr.htm` EX-99.1, which `_pick_release_doc` would otherwise lose to the cover on name shape; the period reference is checked against the primary-doc name as well as the exhibit name (6-K exhibit names carry no period signal); equidistant candidates break ties toward the most release-named primary doc, so SHOP's press-release 6-K beats its same-day results-tables 6-K (whose 99.1 is financial statements, not the narrative release). `_release_name_rank` factored out of `_pick_release_doc`'s nested `_rank` for the tiebreaks; `_quarter_tokens` factored out of `_exhibit_matches_period`. Live backfill: SHOP 7/8 → 8/8 with the real Q3-2024 release ("Internet, Everywhere - November 12, 2024 ... 26% revenue growth and 19% free cash flow margin"). Strictly additive: domestic filers see zero behavior change (6-K anchors are dropped wherever a 10-Q/10-K covers the date; the fallback only runs when no 2.02 match exists).

AGM/BFCM/dividend/annual-report negatives, anchor extraction, 6-K pool, 2.02-pool exclusion, primary-doc exclusion, pressrelease-vs-results tiebreak, unrelated-6-K rejection, end-to-end SHOP-shaped discovery, 10-Q shadowing). ### Batch 104 — footnote-definition legend lines never become the headline (2026-10-20)
Closes the carried "GEV footnote-definition headline wart" follow-up. GEV's Workiva ex-99 opens with a footnote legend block — `1 Defined as remaining performance obligation (RPO)`, `*Non-GAAP Financial Measure`, `Page 1` — before the real headline, and the numeric definition line was picked as the headline (the real headline landed in the lede). **fix** (`data/filings.py`): new `_FOOTNOTE_DEF_RE` skips footnote-definition legend lines in both the headline pass and the lede pass — two narrow shapes: numeric key + definition verb (`1 Defined as ...`, `2 Represents ...`; the verb guards numeric-opening headlines like "2025 outlook raised" / "1Q26 record quarter" / "1 billion in buybacks", which never carry a definition verb) and glyph markers attached to the text (`*Non-GAAP Financial Measure`, `†Excludes ...`; a spaced `* Foo` is prose punctuation, not a legend). Also extended `_ADMIN_LINE_RE` with bare `^page\s+\d+$` ("Page 1" headers — GEV) and lone `^news$` (Southern Company's "News" section kicker, which sat before the contact block and would have become the headline once "Page 1" was skipped; a real headline is never one word). The `^news$` addition was forced by the blast-radius scan: SO's Q2-2024 exhibit carries the same Workiva header shape with a proper headline 10 lines down ("Southern Company reports second-quarter 2024 earnings") that the old code never reached — its stored headline was "Page 1". DB-wide scan: exactly 1 quarter with a footnote-def headline (GEV Q2 FY2025) and 2 with bare "Page 1" (GEV, SO); all others byte-identical. Live repair: cleared the two junk rows and re-ran the enrich — GEV Q2 FY2025 now leads with the real headline + "Second Quarter 2025 Highlights" financial bullets, SO Q2 FY2024 leads with its real headline. Dev-server lesson: `_enrich_press_release_highlights` sets attributes but never commits — the repair script's `db.refresh(row)` without a commit discarded the refill; commit before refresh.

**Tests:** 6 new (regex matches incl. glyph marker; headline-shape negatives incl. "2025 outlook raised", "1Q26 record quarter", "1 billion in buybacks", spaced-asterisk; GEV-shaped end-to-end; SO-shaped kicker end-to-end; NEWS CORP headline not swallowed by the `^news$` rule; lede-pass legend skip). Full suite 887 green, `git diff --check` clean. ### Batch 112 — BRK.B no-headline design + dateline/quarter-label fixes (2026-10-22)
Design decision carried since batch 109, now resolved: Berkshire's earnings releases have **no headline at all** — company name + "NEWS RELEASE" + date + dateline, then the lede. The old extractor stored the company name ("BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC."); the pre-fix code picked the dateline ("Omaha, NE (BRK.A; BRK.B) –"). **Decision: a dateline is never a headline** — when the scan reaches a dateline with no headline found, the honest result is headline=None and the lede starts after the dateline. Two extractor fixes in `data/filings.py`: **(1)** new `_DATELINE_RE` (city + state/country, optional date/parenthetical tickers, trailing em/en dash or hyphen) checked at the generic headline-pick site — dateline reached → `body_start = i + 1`, break, headline stays None; **(2)** `_QUARTER_EARNINGS_LABEL_RE` generalizes the batch-110 "Earnings Release" label branch to quarter-prefixed variants ("FIRST QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RELEASE" — Berkshire heads Q1 releases with it; the batch-110 branches only covered bare and single-token-prefixed labels, so the label became the headline on Q1 2026). Narrow: quarter-word + year + label words, so a genuine "X Schedules First Quarter Earnings Release" headline never matches. ### Batch 121 — derivation-vintage rule: a restated annual must not pair with an unrestated 9M + DB-wide repair (2026-10-24)

Break years still abstain first via the batch-85/120 guard, which runs before this rule.

### Batch 123 — seed round 42 + contact-table headline fix: flattened two-column contact tables are never headlines (2026-10-25)

### Batch 124 — compound earnings-release document title skipped: LULU Q3 headlines repaired (2026-10-25)
Closes the batch-123 carried follow-up: **LULU's Q3 FY2024 and Q3 FY2025 headlines were the 8-K document title "EARNINGS RELEASE & STOCK REPURCHASE PROGRAM" instead of the real release title.** Raw-document investigation showed the shape: lululemon's Q3 releases combine the earnings release with a stock-repurchase announcement in one 8-K, so the exhibit's document title sits before "Exhibit 99.1" while the real headline follows it ("LULULEMON ATHLETICA INC. ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER FISCAL 2024/2025 RESULTS"). Q4 was fine because its title is the bare "EARNINGS RELEASE", which the label branch already skips — the compound form was the unhandled case. Fix in `data/filings.py`: `_is_compound_earnings_title` — when a line carries "earnings release" followed by "&" or "and", an exhibit-marker line ("Exhibit 99.1" / "EX-99.1", new `_EXHIBIT_MARKER_RE`) appears within the next 2 lines, and the line after the marker is a headline-shaped line carrying a headline verb (announces/reports), the title line is skipped and the loop picks the real headline. The guards are each load-bearing: the "&"/"and" requirement keeps bare labels on their existing branch; the marker lookahead keeps a compound title with no marker after it on old behavior; and the verb-headline requirement is what keeps JPMorgan's stored headline safe — its "EARNINGS RELEASE - THIRD QUARTER 2025 RESULTS" title is also followed by an exhibit marker, but the line after the marker is the company name/address block, not a verb headline. A first version of the title regex carried `\b` after `&`, which can never match ("&" followed by a space has no word boundary) — caught by the new tests, fixed to `(&|and\b)`. **Live repair: both LULU Q3 rows re-extracted** — headlines now the real titles, bodies byte-identical apart from the headline itself (+25 chars each); the other 6 LULU quarters unchanged.

**Tests:** 4 new (LULU Q3 end-to-end; "&" and "and" compound forms; helper guard negatives — no marker, prose after marker, bare label, JPM dash-title; JPM-shaped doc keeps its headline). ### Batch 125 — slide-deck bullet-run mega-lines split: BAC 8/8 blank quarters repaired (2026-10-25)
A DB-wide blank-highlights audit (25 of 2394 quarters) found **BAC blank on all 8 quarters** — the only whole-company blank left after batches 92–94. Discovery was fine (all 8 quarters resolve to `bacMMDDYYYYex991.htm` exhibits); the extractor returned None. Root cause: Bank of America's releases are slide decks, and `_html_to_text` flattens a whole highlights slide into a single 7,000-char line with bullets joined by " • " and no line breaks. The headline loop saw one line over the 300-char cap, picked no headline, and the batch-105 page-line guard (no headline + first paragraph > 1000 chars) discarded the release — the exact shape batch 105 deliberately left as "Not available". Fix in `data/filings.py`: `_split_bullet_runs`, applied at the top of `extract_press_release_highlights` before any headline/section/lede logic — a line longer than the headline cap with at least two " • " separators splits into one pseudo-line per bullet, with continuation pieces keeping a "• " prefix so downstream bullet logic (lede bullets, the batch-115 bullet-headline strip) treats them as bullets. Short lines and single-separator lines are untouched. The split's first piece is the deck title ("1 2Q26 Financial Highlights… Business Segment Highlights… Consumer Banking"), so the headline loop also gains a never-headline branch for slide-deck titles (page number + quarter token + "Financial Highlights") — without it the title piece became the headline. Result for BAC Q2 2026: headline "Net income of $3.3 billion" (lead bullet, Palantir precedent — the true "Bank of America Reports…" headline is glued to sub-heads and endnotes inside the final bullet piece with no sentence boundary, so exact recovery would need BAC-specific surgery and is deliberately not attempted) with genuine segment bullets as the body. The bullet-as-headline behavior is load-bearing for Palantir/Skydance tests, so no bullet skip was added to the headline loop. **Live repair: all 8 BAC quarters backfilled** — every quarter now shows real Consumer Banking segment bullets (e.g. Q2 2026: net income $3.3B, revenue $11.3B up 5%); blank cohort drops 25 → 17.

**Tests:** 3 new (mega-line split unit behavior + BAC-shaped end-to-end extraction; deck-title never-headline narrowness). Full suite 1021 green, `git diff --check` clean. **Blast-radius:** the split only fires on >300-char lines with ≥2 " • " separators, so prose releases are byte-identical by construction; the never-headline branch only matches lines starting with a page number + token + "Financial Highlights". Live: /company/BAC overview 200, /company/BAC/detail/data 200 rendering the backfilled "Net income of $3.3 billion" highlights.

### Batch 126 — supplement-only packets are not highlights: EOG's footnote/table garbage becomes honest blanks (2026-10-25)
Closes the batch-125 EOG follow-up, with a corrected mechanism: EOG's exhibits are combined release + supplement packets whose narrative release text lives in full-page JPEG images (7–12 page images per exhibit); the text layer holds only the supplement TOC and tables. The batch-125 note's "TOC entries not skipped" diagnosis was imprecise — the actual paths are twofold. (1) Six exhibits land on a table footnote definition as the headline: the SPG TOC rule over-consumes (every table row is ≤140 chars, and table footers supply the ≥2 page lines), stopping at the first >140-char line, which is a footnote legend — e.g. Q2 2026's "(B)Crude oil and condensate volumes are from UAE and Bahrain operations..." with a Balance Sheets table as the body; Q1 FY2026 stored exactly this shape. (2) Q3 FY2024 lands on the TOC subtitle ("Supplemental Financial and Operating Data Page") with the TOC entries as the body, because its TOC has only one standalone page line so the TOC rule's ≥2-page requirement never fires. Fix in `data/filings.py`, two result-level guards after headline cleanup (deliberately NOT a headline-loop skip — skipping footnote lines in the loop would just move the pick onto a table heading or financial row, since a 700-line table document always yields some pick): a footnote-definition headline (single letter/digit in parentheses, `_FOOTNOTE_HEADLINE_RE`) returns None, and a body consisting entirely (≥2 lines) of title + page-number lines (`_TOC_ENTRY_RE`) returns None. The single-character bound is load-bearing: "(NYSE: ACME)" and "(2026)" parentheticals are not footnote markers and keep working (both covered by tests). The image-page narrative itself is structurally unextractable (same class as SKYD per batch 48) — no OCR is attempted; honest blank beats fabricated highlights. **Live repair: EOG Q1 FY2026's stored footnote-table row cleared to NULL** (highlights + source); all 8 EOG exhibits now extract to None, so the blank cohort goes 17 → 18 with EOG honestly 8/8 blank instead of 7 blank + 1 garbage.

### Batch 134 — subsidiary-list masthead skipped: CINF's 9 subsidiary-line headlines repaired (2026-10-26)
Closes the CINF follow-up carried from batch 120 and deferred in batch 133. ### Batch 135 — fragment-tail headline wraps: CB's 8 stored fragment headlines repaired (2026-10-27)
Closes the CB "Core" follow-up carried from batch 120 (and deferred through batch 134). Root cause in `data/filings.py`: Chubb's release headline is a whole paragraph wrapped at arbitrary points, and the wrap lands mid-phrase on a word no existing tail rule recognized — a modifier awaiting its head noun ("Net Income and Core" / "Operating Income", "P&C Up 10.6% and Life" / "Insurance", "Respectively; Consolidated" / "Net Premiums Written", "P&C Combined" / "Ratio", "Excluding Catastrophe Losses and Prior" / "Period Development") or the preposition "Up" awaiting its figure ("Net Income of $7.35, Up" / "34.6%") — and digit-led percentage continuations ("21.7%;", "85.2%;") were refused outright by the digit-led bad-start guard, stranding the figure as the first body line. The old joiner stored only the first line ("Chubb Reports Second Quarter Per Share Net Income and Core") and left the rest of the headline paragraph as body lines. Fix: `_HEADLINE_FRAGMENT_TAIL_RE` (Core/Record/Consolidated/Life/Net/Operating/Combined/Prior/P&C/Up — each a word that cannot end a complete headline), `_HEADLINE_PCT_LEAD_RE` (percentage-led continuations bypass the digit guard only after a fragment or wrap tail — never after a verb/ordinal tail, where a digit-led line is a metric-table row), and the join cap rises 3 → 12 (CB's longest paragraph needs 10 joins; every join still requires a trigger plus all continuation guards). One guard against the new tail's weakest case: a fragment-tail join is blocked when the continuation is itself a fresh headline — Danaher's cover slogan "Innovation at the speed of life" ends on "life" but is followed by "Danaher Reports … Results", and joining them would build a Franken-headline (the guard was proven by a pre-guard run that produced exactly that on all 12 DHR quarters; post-guard DHR is byte-identical). **Live repair: all 8 stored CB rows re-extracted** — 6 now carry the full headline paragraph (e.g. Q2 2024, 58 → 418 chars; Q4 2025, 60 → 525 chars), 2 partial: Q3 2024 stops at "…Net Investment Income" (the "Both Up Double-Digit…" lines stay in the body — nothing lost), Q4 2024 stops at "…and Life Insurance" (its tail clause "Up 15.7%; P&C Combined Ratio of 86.6%" drops out of the stored text: the orphan line between the headline paragraph and the bullets is dropped by the section extractor — a future "Insurance"-tail rule recovers it into the headline; the trade buys the full bullet body, which the old 6-line lede never reached).

**Tests:** 4 new (CB Q2 2024 end-to-end full-paragraph join; "Up" + percentage-continuation chain; guard negatives — sentence-terminated lede after a fragment tail, digit-led line after a verb tail, bullet after a fragment tail, complete "Record Growth" headline untouched; DHR slogan fresh-headline block + Merck wrap-comma exemption). ### Batch 136 — "for"-led headline continuations: MCO/FICO/KR/ROST period phrases joined; 24 stale AND-continuation rows repaired (2026-10-27)
Root cause in `data/filings.py`: some filers wrap the headline mid-phrase with the period phrase leading the second line — "MOODY'S CORPORATION REPORTS RESULTS" / "FOR THIRD QUARTER 2025", "FICO Announces Earnings of $7.40 per Share" / "for Third Quarter Fiscal 2025", "... Announces Guidance" / "for 2026", "ROSS STORES REPORTS RESULTS" / "FOR FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL 2024" — and batch 107's conjunction-lead rule only recognized and/or/but, so the period phrase was stored as the first body line and the headline read as if it had no period at all. Fix: `_HEADLINE_FOR_LEAD_RE` — a "for" lead is a trigger only with a period designator (ordinal quarter, or a bare year standing alone on its line). The narrowness is the point: a bare "for" lead is NOT a trigger, because lede "For ..." lines are common — but they always start "For the ..." ("For the three months ended ...:", "For the full year:") or are admin lines ("For 6:00 a.m. ET Release"), and the (?!the\b) guard plus the $-anchored bare year ("For 2026, the company expects ..." never matches) keep all three guard shapes out. **Live repair: 37 stored rows** — 13 FOR rows (MCO 3, FICO 8, KR 1, ROST 1) plus 24 stale AND-continuation rows (NKE, UNH, SPG, ARCC, HON, UPS, GIS, SJM, CVS, MPC) whose stored headlines predate the batch-107 AND rule and were never repaired: 23 by full live re-extraction (live body agrees with stored body up to paragraph grouping/bullet spacing and trailing extras), 14 by headline-splice (new headline + stored body byte-preserved) where the live body diverges for non-headline reasons — UNH Q2's live text drops the stored CEO-quote tail, UPS's live bullets re-space a "*", ARCC's table-section tail and MCO's section pick differ — so the splice fixes the headline without silently rewriting or losing body content. One row deliberately skipped: CART's "And price parity ..." is a genuine body sentence (live extraction None), not a continuation.

**Tests:** 5 new (MCO Q3 2025 end-to-end; FICO quarter-fiscal join; ROST quarter-and-fiscal join; KR bare-year join; guard negatives — Realty Income/Intuit colon labels, Lowe's admin line, "For the first quarter, revenue ..." lede, "For 2026, the company expects ..." outlook sentence). Post-repair scan finds exactly 1 cohort row left (CART, by design). ### Batch 139 — Lede-budget separators: lone bullet markers never consume budget in marker-delimited ledes; CB Q3 2024 trailing bullets closed, 13 stored rows repaired (2026-10-27)
Closes the batch-138 CB Q3 follow-up — but the mechanism turned out to be the budget accounting, not the cap size. Root cause in `data/filings.py`: the lede fallback's 6-line budget counted every line, including lone bullet-marker separators — and Chubb's Q3 2024 markers ("·" middle dot, "○" white circle) were not even in `_is_lone_bullet_marker`, so the lead "·" was kept as a junk paragraph and the budget ran out after bullet 2 ("·" + 3 bullet-1 lines + "·" + bullet-2 line = 6), although the lede holds 8 bullets; the stored row (older extraction) held bullet 1 only. Fix, in the lede loop only: (1) "·" and "○" join the lone-marker predicate (lead markers of either kind are skipped, mid-lede ones kept as separator paragraphs); (2) markers never consume budget; (3) in a marker-delimited lede the current item is finished rather than cut mid-item — up to 4 continuation lines past the budget, and a marker at the boundary ends collection without being appended (no dangling marker). The finish rule is gated on a marker having been seen: a marker-less prose lede keeps the old hard 6-line cap, because without item delimiters "finish the item" is undefined — the ungated version changed 109/232 blast quarters (mostly prose extensions up to the 4000-char cap and table-row drift on ARCC) for no defect, and the gate is what rejected it. **Live repair: 13 stored rows** (CB 7 incl. ### Batch 140 — Lone bullet markers are never stored: lede, section, and leading-block paths all drop them; predicate gains "▪"/"–"; 27 marker rows + 3 page rows remain gated-out (2026-10-27)
DB-wide audit of stored highlights found the junk class batch 138/139 left behind: 42 rows with a lone-marker paragraph (lede path — SPG/NUE/CB/CI/SNPS/SLB/GIS/KVUE/ON/NDAQ/VRSK/UNP), 50 rows with a lone-marker line inside a "\n"-joined paragraph (section path and leading-bullet-block path — Nucor's "•" per item, PNC's "▪", Simon's "–"), and 9 rows carrying "Page N of M" artifacts (4 bare MET paragraphs; UNH's inline "Page 1 of 16 <headline>" page-image mega-lines are a different shape and stay out of scope). Root cause in `data/filings.py`: batch 139 kept mid-lede markers as separator paragraphs on the theory that they separate bullets in the rendered output — but paragraphs are already blank-line separated, so a lone marker paragraph renders as a junk glyph line and adds no separation; the section collector and the leading bullet block never filtered markers at all. Fix, in all three paths: the lede loop no longer appends lone markers (marker_seen is still set, so the batch-139 finish rule and budget behavior are unchanged); the section collector and the leading bullet block drop lone-marker lines AFTER qualification, so their caps and floors see the same lines as before. The predicate gains the last two glyphs the audit found standing alone: "▪" (PNC) and "–" en dash (Simon — the hyphen-minus was covered, the en dash was not). This supersedes batch 138's "applying the skips to the section path or _leading_bullet_block" deliberately-not-done (that decision predated the audit evidence) and batch 139's keep-as-separator choice; 3 batch-139 expectations and 1 batch-138 expectation were updated to the new decision. **Live repair:** every row passing the gate was written (final round: SPG 2024-12-31, SPG 2025-12-31); the repair only ever removes junk paragraphs/lines, never imports live content — so SPG 2025-12-31's budget-freed FFO line (see blast note) is NOT in the stored row, same precedent as batch 137's untaken trailing bullets. ### Batch 146 — Flattened summary-table mode parses Airbnb's heading-less shareholder-letter table into bullets; 6 stored ABNB rows repaired (2026-10-28)
Closes the batch-143 follow-up "ABNB heading-less metric table". Root cause in `data/filings.py`: the batch-94 metric mode requires a "Highlights" heading line, which Airbnb's letter never has — its summary table ("Key Financial Measures" / "Key Business Metrics") sits at the document head, and text extraction flattens it into run-on lines (group-header words split around the first metric's value, "Revenue Key Financial $3.6B Measures"; wrapped labels split around their value, "Free Cash $1.3B Flow ("FCF")*"; Q4 letters carry quarter + full-year value columns), so the standard path served the flattened table as headline + prose. Fix: a third shareholder-letter mode, tried after the batch-94 metric mode and before the standard path, that parses the value-delimited token stream — label value [change …] — where a change phrase is "%" + "Y/Y" ["(ex-FX)"] or "%" + words ending in "margin"; a between-values piece splits into label continuation (before the first %, or up to the first parenthetical when there is no %), change phrases, and the next label; consecutive values merge into multi-column values, and a detected dual-column header ("Q4 2025; FY 2025") names the value order. Two implementation findings from the first failing runs: the table-start search must match the header fragment ("key financial"/"key business"), not the full phrase, because the split header never appears contiguously on one line; and a footnote star after a parenthetical belongs to the continuation, not the next label ("* Trailing Twelve Month" was the first-run symptom). Anything that does not fit the grammar fails the whole parse, so the old behavior is preserved — in particular the Q3/Q4 2024 letters, whose table cells interleave with narrative sentences, fail on the first prose change phrase ("10% compared to Q3 2023…") instead of emitting junk labels.

### Batch 148 — Bounded `_skip_toc` tail: a TOC followed directly by narrative no longer loses its headline; 0 live quarters change (2026-10-29)
Closes the standing `_skip_toc` over-consumption follow-up carried since batch 126. Root cause in `data/filings.py`: after the last page-number line, the skip consumed title-shaped lines without limit, so a combined packet whose narrative follows the TOC directly (short headline + short ledes, no Contacts: block, no >140-char line) lost its headline — demonstrated end-to-end, old code stored the first medium-length prose sentence ("Management highlighted broad-based strength in leasing and occupancy ...") as the headline. Fix: the tail after the last page number is bounded — when its first headline-shaped line appears (headline verb + results topic, no terminal sentence punctuation), the skip rolls back to that line, skipping any leading footnote marker with the tail (landing on "(1)" would trip the footnote-headline guard and lose the release); a tail with no headline-shaped line keeps the old return, so SPG's "(1)" + footnote + mini-TOC tail is byte-identical. ### Batch 153 — Lede/section table skip: outlook tables no longer fill the highlights; 11 stored rows repaired (2026-10-30)
Closes the batch-149/150/151/152 follow-up "CCI lede tail-trim rule candidate" and the "CCI bullet-vs-lede gap" — and the APP guidance-heading tail from batch 152. Root cause, found by probing the live exhibits rather than the stored rows: Crown Castle opens its releases with the outlook table directly after the dateline paragraph, so the lede loop filled its 6-line budget with the table itself (unit line, outlook-table headings, header lines, data rows) and the real highlights bullets after the table starved. The stored rows were the better half of the defect (real bullet + 2-line wart tail); the live extraction was worse (table headers as the whole body). The fix skips table lines in the lede loop — they neither consume budget nor get stored — so the prose after the table is collected instead; a trailing table run is trimmed after collection; and the leading-bullet block and the Highlights-section collector both end at a table heading instead of swallowing it (AppLovin's "First Quarter 2026 Financial Guidance Summary" heading after the bullets).

**Predicates (the hard part was wrapped prose):** `_html_to_text` keeps literal newlines inside block elements, so a long paragraph arrives as unterminated mid-sentence fragments — "fiscal 2026 second quarter results with total revenue of $16.0 billion, up 8% in" looks exactly like an unterminated $-carrying line, and the first version of the skip ate Oracle/Chubb/USB wrapped fragments (5 test failures). The final predicates are strict about that: data rows must be figure-dense (2+ figures, ≥40% of tokens; a standalone "%" counts so spaced-out "67 %" rows qualify; the figure regex never matches a lone comma, which had made Chubb bullet fragments score as figure-dense); outlook/guidance headings must be pure header vocabulary (a prose clause mentioning the outlook fails on its verbs); period/date headers must be all period/date tokens with a year or month present; labels must be short and never $-carrying ("$50.2 billion" is a metric value, kept); terminated lines and bullets are never table lines. A trailing bare highlights heading ("Additional Financial Highlights:" whose bullets never arrived) is trimmed the same way.

**Tests:** 5 new (CCI-shaped lede skip incl. wordy data-row label, 9-word period header, and all-caps section heading; APP guidance-summary tail in the lede and in the section and leading-block paths; direct predicate checks incl. spaced-% rows, date headers, and the wrapped-prose negatives). ### Batch 154 — Space-less bullets are bullets: the bullet regex no longer requires a space, so Highlights sections stop being rejected as tables; 5 stored rows repaired (2026-10-30)
Closes the CCI bullet-vs-lede gap for the last affected quarter (Q3 2024) and the CART Q2 FY2026 tail wart from batch 153. Root cause, found by tracing why the live extraction for CCI Q3 2024 returned the lede instead of the 7-bullet "HIGHLIGHTS FROM THE QUARTER" section: `_BULLET_LEAD_RE` required a whitespace after the bullet glyph, but flattened exhibits emit "•Site rental revenues." with the text glued to the glyph — a DB sweep finds space-less bullet lines in 1118 of 2439 stored bodies across ~180 tickers, so this is the dominant bullet shape, not a CCI quirk. The missed guard defeated the batch-107 bullet guard in `_looks_like_financial_table`: 3 space-less $+%-carrying CCI bullets plus the $+%-carrying CFO quote tripped the data_rows >= 4 threshold, the genuine section was rejected as a financial table, and the lede fallback served the outlook table instead. The same failure discarded Instacart's financial Highlights sections, so the business section won and the batch-102 financial priority never fired for CART. The fix lets the glyph bullets (•/●/–/—) stand without a following space; the hyphen stays strict (space required) so a "-$1,234" negative table value still counts as a data row. The same regex guards all five use sites (table check, table-cell check, lede table-line, lede tail continuation). ### Batch 155 — Mixed-case datelines break the leading-bullet block; "(unaudited)"-suffixed Highlights headings leak table scaffolding; 8 GOOGL rows repaired (2026-10-30)
Closes the GOOGL table-fragment cohort carried since batch 154 — but the batch-154 premise was wrong in one respect, and the repair gates caught it: live extraction was NOT already clean for all 8 quarters. Root cause, found by tracing the Q4 exhibit through the extractor's pieces: `_DATELINE_LEAD_RE` required all-caps location segments, but Alphabet's dateline is "MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. – February 4, 2025 – ..." — the mixed-case state ("Calif.") never matched, so `_leading_bullet_block` broke at the dateline (first body line, not a bullet) and returned None. Q1–Q3 hid the failure because the lede fallback still served dateline + bullets; Q4 exposed it because the "Q4 2024 Financial Highlights" table section was the only section candidate and won by the earliest-candidate rule. The fix allows mixed case in both location segments of `_DATELINE_LEAD_RE` (the comma + capital-led state + spaced-dash shape still keeps prose out: no digits in the class, so a "Q4"-led line never matches, and a lowercase-led second segment never matches). A second change, surfaced by the blast: `_HIGHLIGHTS_HEADING_RE` now allows a trailing parenthetical after the closing word ("Q1 2025 Financial Highlights (unaudited)") — Alphabet suffixes Q1/Q2 2025's headings that way, and without it the leading block swallowed the heading plus the table-intro sentence as a bullet continuation (the first blast showed the 2-line wart on both quarters). The batch-97 guard is preserved: "Highlights" must still head or close the line, so a mid-sentence "highlight" verb in footnotes still never matches.

### Batch 158 — Multi-line CEO quotes finish in the leading-bullet block; closing-quote terminal check drops JNJ table-heading residue; 8 stale stored rows repaired (2026-10-30)
Closes the multi-line-quote follow-up carried since batch 155. In `_leading_bullet_block`, the item-close rule broke the block at the first line ending in terminal punctuation — but a multi-line CEO quote's opener ends mid-quote ("Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said: “Our AI investments are redefining what's possible across every part of our business."), so GOOGL Q2 FY2026's stored highlights ended at that sentence and the remaining three quote lines never served. Two helpers now judge the close: `_item_has_open_quote` scans the current item's quote state (curly quotes nest by depth, a straight `"` toggles, mixed forms compose), and `_current_leading_item_text` scopes that state to the current item so an earlier item's closed quote can't keep a later item open. While the quote is open the break is skipped; the 14-line cap and the heading/boilerplate breaks above still bound the block, so an unclosed quote cannot run away. A second change in the same `if`: the terminal-punctuation regex now sees through a closing quote (`.”` / `."` count as terminal). The old regex never matched a line ending in `”`, so a quote that opened and closed on one line never closed the item itself — the next prose line leaked in before the rule fired. That leak is what put JNJ's "Overall financial results" / "Q4" table headings into stored bodies: JNJ's dateline paragraph is one mega-line ending `...technology.”`, and the old code appended the table's header lines as continuations before the table-units break stopped it.

The regression is pinned by stashing the src change: the old code truncates the shaped block to 3 lines ending mid-quote with no closing quote, and the new tests fail to import (the helpers don't exist). The other 109 quarters are byte-identical, including all shareholder-letter, image-only, and Tesla quarters. **Live repair: 8 stored rows replaced** under the batch-157 gates (re-fetched inside the repair script; live source label equals stored; live ≥200 chars; headline match; every stored bullet core + terminated stored sentence survives; live carries no table residue — the removed JNJ lines are unterminated headings under the 30-char narrative floor, so they pass the gate by design): GOOGL Q3 FY2024 (965 → 1547), Q4 FY2025 (1524 → 2209), Q1 FY2026 (1872 → 2222), Q2 FY2026 (1146 → 2148), Q3 FY2026 (1145 → 1994); JNJ Q4 FY2025 (1868 → 1832), Q1 FY2026 (1774 → 1675), Q2 FY2026 (1787 → 1752). ### Batch 166 — Footnote-definition blocks skip as blocks; 4 stale EMR rows repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-165 follow-up in full — the multi-line footnote skipper is now the single gate for the whole hazard class, at all four collection paths (headline loop, lede, leading-bullet block, Highlights sections) plus the salvage path's sentence check. **fix** (`data/filings.py`): `_footnote_def_block_len(lines, i)` returns how many lines the footnote-definition block starting at `lines[i]` occupies, or 0. Openers: the three single-line shapes, the bracketed shape (`[1] Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure.` — Coinbase's Q2 FY2025 letter served its [1]/[2] footnotes as the lede), the fourth shape (numeric key + bare capitalized term, definition verb on the next line: `1 Coinbase Total Trading Volume / comprises Spot Trading Volume`), and the same-line term+verb variant (`3 Trading Volume represents the`, `4 Crypto Asset Volatility represents`, `1 Spot Trading Volume is` — the last one is why shape 2 misses it: its participle is "presented", outside shape 2's list; a bare `is`/`are` counts only at line end or before a definition participle, so `1 Total Revenue is expected to grow` never opens). The term's first word must be Title-Case but later words may be lowercase (Emerson's `2 Underlying orders do not include AspenTech.`, `2 Underlying sales exclude/excludes the impact ...`), with an optional `do not / does not` before the verb. Consumption: only sentence termination ends a definition — there is deliberately no completeness gate (a wrapped line can look complete: `[3] $USD resources is defined as cash and cash` carries a 5-word object yet wraps onto `equivalents and USDC ...`); an unterminated line consumes its next line only when it is a plausible wrap (lowercase-led, definition-verb-led, conjunction-led, a `U.S.`-style abbreviation lead, a `US`-style all-caps lead, a `$`/digit-led figure line, or a bare-term opener — a year-led sentence `2025 was a strong year ...` is never a wrap). After a definition terminates, the block chains only onto another definition opener. Hard boundaries are structural only (bullets, boilerplate, admin/contact, headings, datelines) — table predicates were removed from the boundary after the blast showed figure-dense continuations (`million and $687 million in pre-tax gains ...`) scoring as table lines and stopping the block at the key line. The headline loop takes `include_paren=False`: a paren line stays headline-eligible there (batch 126 — `(B)Crude oil ...` headlines a supplement packet that must return None; `(2026) ACME CORP ...` headlines are preserved). The lede also drops investor-conference-call notices (`conference call` + `webcast`/`replay`, singular `call` with a word boundary — AppLovin's `Webcast and Conference Calls` heading is plural and is not a notice). **Blast-radius story:** the first blast showed 12 diffs — 6 EOG (the headline loop was skipping paren lines, defeating the batch-126 supplement guard) and 6 COIN/EMR; the `include_paren` fix cleared all 6 EOG diffs. The second blast showed the COIN footnote tails still served (the boundary bug + the completeness gate) and the EMR call-notice backfill; the boundary/completeness fixes plus the call-notice exclusion and the `US`-lead/`excludes?` refinements left exactly 7 diffs, all intended: EMR ×4 (footnote tails only) and COIN ×3 (footnote text out; the rounding paragraph now fills the lede). A third blast confirmed the APP false positive was gone (`Webcast and Conference Calls` heading no longer matches the notice regex). **Live repair: 4 stored rows replaced** under the batch-157 gates (re-fetched inside the repair script; live source label equals stored; live ≥200 chars; stored headline kept verbatim; every stored bullet core + terminated stored sentence survives; live carries no table residue and no call notice; repair live text byte-identical to the blast's new extraction for all 4): EMR 2024-12-31 (1816 → 1710, `1 Results are presented...` + `2 Underlying orders...` out), EMR 2025-03-31 (2382 → 2339, `1 Results are presented...` out), EMR 2025-12-31 (1535 → 1377, both `1`/`2` Underlying lines out), EMR 2026-03-31 (1449 → 1359, both lines out). ### Batch 167 — Rounding-note + asterisk-note skips; quarter titles are headlines; 3 stale COIN rows repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-166 COIN follow-ups in full. Coinbase's letters carry a rounding boilerplate paragraph ahead of the letter prose — the long form ("Figures have been rounded for presentation purposes only. For additional financial information and a reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP results, please refer to the reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP results table(s) in this shareholder letter and our Form 10-K/10-Q filed with the SEC on <date>.") and the short form ("Note: Figures presented [above] may not sum precisely due to rounding."). **fix** (`data/filings.py`): `_rounding_note_block_len` skips the note as a block at all four collection paths (headline loop, lede, leading-bullet block, Highlights sections) plus a sentence-level check in the salvage path. Consumption runs to sentence termination taking any non-boundary line as a continuation — unlike the footnote block, a note's wraps are ordinary sentence fragments ("GAAP results table in this shareholder letter and our", "Coinbase's Class A common stock", "Form 10-Q filed with the SEC on May 8, 2025."), so the footnote block's plausibility test would stop the block mid-note and serve the rest; the opener is the guard instead (both regexes match boilerplate only). After termination the block chains only onto "For additional financial information" (the long form's second sentence, for when the sentence break falls on a line boundary); a following note is its own opener. The same batch adds the orphaned-sentence form as an opener: Q3 FY2024 carries the short note plus the referral sentence with no long-form first sentence, so the referral paragraph was served as lede content. **fix:** `_asterisk_note_block_len` skips chart asterisk notes ("* Based on the closing price of Coinbase's Class A common stock on May 7, 2025 on the Nasdaq Global Stock Market.", "*Below reporting threshold of 10%.", "*Net of USDC loaned or pledged as collateral.", "*As of December 31, 2024, USDC excludes ...", "* Measures used in this release ...") as blocks at the same four paths. The lede's table-line rule already dropped the opener, but its wrapped continuations were served — "Coinbase's Class A common stock" opened Q1 FY2025's lede once the rounding note was skipped — and in the leading-bullet block the opener starts a bullet item. The lead list is deliberately note-shaped (Based on / As of / Net of / Below / Measures used): a highlights bullet never opens with one, and the batch-165 "* Revenue grew 12 percent." bullet stays a bullet. **fix:** quarter titles are headlines, not masthead material — "First Quarter 2025" / "Second Quarter 2025" were skipped twice over: `_looks_like_masthead_residue` swallowed the 3-word form as a street / city-postal line (≤4 words + digit) and the headline loop's masthead branch skipped it when the date line followed, and `_skip_bare_masthead_name` read it as a company name (the date + page number count as residue and the first footnote line — "[1] Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial", unterminated, so headline-shaped — counts as the real headline). Q1 survived by luck: its "[1] This is a non-GAAP financial measure." ends with a period, so the bare-masthead lookahead returned None. Both skips now exclude quarter titles (`_QUARTER_TITLE_RE`: "First/Second/Third/Fourth Quarter [and Full Year] YYYY"), so the title is picked as the headline — the same shape Q4's "Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024" already had. The design considered a fallback ("use the skipped title when no other headline is found") and rejected it: with the title skipped, the loop would pick the letter's first prose sentence as a Franken-headline ("We delivered strong financial results in Q1, ... Fellow Shareholders,") via the wrap joiner, so the fallback would have to fire on prose-shaped picks — stopping the skip is cleaner and the blast proves no title steals a real verb headline in the cohort. **Live repair: 3 stored rows replaced** under the batch-157 gates with the batch-164 defect-body branch (the stored body IS the defect — rounding note + footnote text — so no stored bullet core or sentence is required to survive; the gates are headline kept verbatim + the live body opens with the letter prose + no rounding/footnote/asterisk residue): COIN 2024-12-31 (322 → 776, rounding paragraph → letter prose), COIN 2025-03-31 (457 → 1119, metric bullet + MTU footnote → letter prose), COIN 2025-06-30 (246 → 678, "[1]/[2]" footnote text → letter prose). ### Batch 168 — Footnote second sentences + paren wrap tails; COIN Q3 FY2024 repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-167 COIN Q3 FY2024 follow-up in full. The stored Q3 FY2024 row was the title + rounding note + the [1] footnote itself, and its live text served two footnote residues. **fix 1** (`data/filings.py`): `_footnote_def_block_len` gains an anaphoric second-sentence chain — after a definition terminates, the next line is consumed as part of the block when it opens with an anaphoric determiner (These/This/Those/That/Both/Such) whose noun appears in the definition just consumed ("These losses were $92 million / after reflecting the tax impact." — "losses" is in the [1] definition's first sentence). A capital-led sentence after a terminated definition is otherwise indistinguishable from new prose, so the noun test is the guard; it is exact, not stemmed, and the definition's words accumulate across its wrapped lines (the noun sits on a wrap line, not the key line). The second sentence's own wraps consume by the normal plausibility rules, and the chain then resumes onto the next definition opener, so the whole [1]/[2]/[3] legend drops as one 12-line block. (Q4 FY2024's identical shape escapes only because its second sentence starts mid-line, "These gains were" sharing the termination line.) **fix 2:** `_is_plausible_continuation` gains a parenthetical abbreviation branch — a line starting with 2+ all-caps letters opening a lowercase parenthetical ("USDC (net of USDC lent or", the [3] definition's wrap tail) is a plausible wrap. The 4-cap lead failed the 2–3-cap abbreviation branch; unlike that branch the termination guard is dropped, because a tail that terminates on its own line ("USDC (net of USDC lent or pledged as collateral).") is still the same definition's tail. The no-digits guard keeps figure-led prose out, and the line is only ever reached as the wrap of an unterminated definition. **Live repair: 1 stored row replaced** under the batch-157 gates with the batch-164 defect-body branch: COIN 2024-09-30 (210 → 493, title + rounding note + [1] footnote → letter prose under the "Third Quarter 2024" headline). The repair's live text is byte-identical to the blast's new extraction. ### Batch 169 — Shareholder-letter salutations skip as blocks; page-line guard bounds the longest line, not the paragraph; 5 stale rows repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-167 COIN Q3 FY2025 greeting-wart follow-up and the NFLX/AXON salutation cohort. Shareholder letters open "Fellow shareholders," / "Dear Shareholders," after the date — a greeting, never highlights — and it was served three ways: as the HEADLINE (NFLX — the headline loop picks the first short line it reaches, so 8 quarters carried the salutation as their headline), as lede content (COIN Q3 FY2025's split "Fellow" / "Shareholders," form, SKYD mid-body — twice in Q1 FY2026), and as a leading-bullet continuation (AXON — the salutation follows the last bullet and the block appends it as a wrap). **fix** (`data/filings.py`): `_salutation_block_len` skips the salutation as a block at all four collection paths (headline loop, lede, leading-bullet block, Highlights sections). In the headline loop a salutation means the letter has no headline at all (NFLX: date / salutation / bullets), so the lede starts after it, like the dateline branch. The pattern is deliberately salutation-shaped: an optional single capitalized word between the opener and "shareholders" ("Fellow Affirm Shareholders,") and an optional trailing comma or period — and the line must END at the salutation. A prose sentence that happens to mention shareholders ("Shareholders approved the merger") never matches, and an inline salutation ("Dear Shareholders, This is my first letter ...", Instacart/Affirm's flattened form) never matches either: dropping that line would eat the prose with it, so those stay served. **fix 2:** the page-line guard's 1000-char bound is on the longest LINE in the first paragraph, not the paragraph — the section path joins a bullet list with "\n", so a 1385-char bullet list read as one paragraph although no line exceeds 350 chars. NFLX Q3 FY2024 exposed it: once headline-less (salutation no longer the headline), its 5-bullet list was discarded as a "page-line" and live went None. ### Batch 170 — "◦" sub-bullets are bullet starts in the leading-bullet block; 7 stale NFLX rows repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-169 carried follow-up in full. Netflix nests "◦" (white bullet, U+25E6) sub-bullets under "•" items in its shareholder letters, and the leading-bullet block truncated at the first one: a "◦" line was appended as a wrap continuation of the "•" item, ended with terminal punctuation, and the next line was another "◦" line — not a "•"/"-"/"*" start — so the item-close rule fired and the block broke, losing every bullet after the first sub-bullet (NFLX Q4 FY2024 live was 204 chars: one "•" item + one "◦" line; the stored row is 801 chars). **fix** (`data/filings.py`): `_LEADING_BULLET_STARTS = ("•", "-", "*", "◦")` — "◦" is a bullet start in the block's item-start check, its item-close next-line check, and `_current_leading_item_text` (so the open-quote check judges the current item from the last "◦" line, not across it). One shared tuple so the three sites cannot drift again. Distinct from "○" (white circle, U+25CB), which the lone-marker rule already covers. **Live repair: 7 stored rows replaced** under the batch-157 gates plus the batch-169 stored-core-preservation gate: NFLX 2024-12-31 (801 → 1494), 2025-03-31 (1134 → 1456), 2025-09-30 (929 → 1442), 2025-12-31 (636 → 1340), 2026-03-31 (1332 → 1606), 2026-06-30 (767 → 1644), 2026-09-30 (308 → 1714 — re-repairs batch 169's own row, which the new code made stale again by serving the full list). ### Batch 173 — Tail guards: footnote pointers, bare-numbered footnotes, role lines, legends, "Key Points:" (2026-11-01)

A dateline sentence carries real narrative (AAPL's carries revenue $94.9B / EPS $0.97; 70 stored rows serve a dateline sentence as lede line 1 — DIS, SHOP, CSX, MCO, DELL). A bare-only skip would change 0 quarters in the corpus, and prefix-stripping was rejected (130 rows of churn for cosmetic gain, no budget freed). **Fix** (`data/filings.py`), at all three collection paths — lede loop, leading-bullet block, and Highlights sections (the section path matters: Walmart's legend only surfaced through its Third-Quarter Highlights section, which the lede-path tests never exercised): (1) `_FOOTNOTE_POINTER_RE` — `^\d{1,3}[.)]?\s+(See|Refer to)\b` — a footnote-definition opener, plus a parenthesized alternative `^\(+(See|Refer to)\b` for Carnival's "(See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” and “Reconciliation of Forecasted Data”)" tail pointer. ### Batch 175 — Trane Wingdings "l" bullets + bare-dollar units line; TT ×7 repaired (2026-11-01)
Closes the batch-174 TT ×7 follow-up in full. **Cause chain:** Trane renders its highlight bullets as a Wingdings "l" glyph (`<font face="Wingdings">l</font>`), which flattens to a lone "l" ("l Reported revenues of $5.4 billion ...") — `_BULLET_LEAD_RE` (•●–—/-) never matched it, so the bullets were invisible to every bullet guard. Worse, the summary table's units line ("$, millions except EPS Q3 2024 Q3 2023 ...") has no parens, so neither units regex matched it (`_TABLE_UNITS_RE` requires `(`, `_TABLE_WORD_UNITS_RE` requires `(in`), and the Highlights section collector ran past the units line and served the table's data rows ("Bookings $5,213 $4,946 5% 5%", "Net Revenues $5,441 ...", "GAAP Operating Income $819 ...") as highlights — 5 of the 7 quarters. The figure-dense EPS bullet ("l GAAP continuing EPS of $3.43; adjusted continuing EPS* of $3.37, up 21 percent", 2 $ figures in 78 chars) was also misflagged as a data row by `_is_lede_data_row`'s $-figures branch, because that predicate had no bullet exemption (unlike `_is_lede_table_line`). Seed-time Q1/Q2 headlines were truncated at "Results;" while live carries the full "Results and Raises ... Guidance" headline. **Fix** (`data/filings.py`): (1) `_BULLET_LEAD_RE` gains `l\s` — the space stays required, so a line starting with the letter "l" as a word ("lower revenue ...") never matches (no English word is a lone "l"); this also exempts "l" bullets in `_is_lede_table_line` and stops them counting as data rows in `_looks_like_financial_table`. (2) `_TABLE_UNITS_RE` gains a bare-dollar alternative `^\$\s*,\s*(millions|thousands|billions)\b` — a line starting "$," plus a scale word is a units header, never prose; one definition, all call sites (section collector, leading-bullet block, `_is_lede_table_line`, `_looks_like_table_fragment`) inherit it. (3) `_is_lede_data_row` exempts bullet-led lines at the top — a highlight bullet is narrative, never a table row, and the predicate itself must say so or direct callers (repair residue scans, `_is_lede_table_label`'s next-line check) misflag figure-dense bullets. **Repair** (`scripts/batch175_repair.py`, TT-only, same gates as batch 174 plus two extensions): stored table-residue lines are defect lines for the preservation gates (the extractor's own `_is_lede_table_line` — bullets never match it, so a dropped bullet still trips the gate), and a live headline is accepted when the stored headline is a strict prefix of it (the truncated seed headline). **7/7 repaired, 0 skipped** — TT 2024-09-30 (1154→797), 2025-03-31 (1132→804), 2025-06-30 (1135→782), 2025-09-30 (1200→843), 2025-12-31 (1224→1004), 2026-03-31 (1174→822), 2026-06-30 (1176→860); all verified in the DB. TT 2024-12-31 was probed and is live == stored (1034 chars) under the new extractor — correctly not a target. The probe/diagnose/blast scripts are left untracked in `scripts/` (`batch175_probe_tt.py`, `batch175_cache_blast.py`, `batch175_repair.py`, `batch175_pred_probe.py`) per the batch-105–110 precedent.

### Batch 176 — Paren footnote false positives drop real prose; ANET/MRK/PLUG lines rescued; FIS ×1 repaired (2026-11-02)
The batch-174 audit remainder (34 rows / 37 lines) split on re-probe into stale data and live extractor gaps. **Cause chain:** the paren footnote shape (`^\([a-z0-9]+\)`, batch 97) is the loosest marker — it also matches a parenthesized abbreviation that a wrapped sentence breaks on. Three attested: Arista's bullet wraps mid-parenthetical ("... multi-planar leaf-spine design" / "(MRC) protocol, and segment routing over IPv6 (SRv6), aimed at maximizing AI cluster utilization and resilience."); Plug's bullet wraps on its abbreviation ("... improved by 25% quarter-over-quarter" / "(QoQ) and 46% year-over-year (YoY), driven by margin expansion ..."); Merck's sentence wraps on its abbreviation ("... compared to intravenous" / "(IV) KEYTRUDA. Merck also announced the initiation of waveLINE-010 ..."). The Highlights section collector dropped all three as footnote-definition blocks — fresh extraction of ANET served a bullet with its tail cut off while the stored row still had it, the regression proof. **Fix** (`data/filings.py`): new `_is_paren_prose_continuation`, wired into `_opens_footnote_def`'s paren branch only — a paren-led line whose post-marker text starts lowercase (a sentence resuming mid-flow) or whose first sentence is a single 2+ letter alphabetic word with a new sentence after it ("(IV) KEYTRUDA." — a bare term, not a definition) is prose, not a footnote definition. The previous line is deliberately NOT consulted: a genuine definition can follow an unterminated table row (Lilly's "(1) Tirzepatide is marketed ..." follows the revenue table's last row), so a prev-line test would keep real footnotes. **Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** `_HIGHLIGHTS_HEADING_RE`'s leading branch is narrowed from bare `^highlights?\b` to heading-shaped tails (`of|from|for|include` + unterminated rest) — the old form matched ANY line starting with the word, so Chipotle's all-caps sub-headlines ("HIGHLIGHTS RETURN TO POSITIVE COMPARABLE SALES AND TRANSACTIONS IN JUNE", Q2 2025; "HIGHLIGHTS POSITIVE COMPARABLE SALES", Q3 2025) were dropped everywhere the regex means "heading". Full-cache survey of every `^highlights` line (17 distinct): the narrowed rule keeps all real headings (bare "Highlights"/"HIGHLIGHTS", "HIGHLIGHTS OF SEGMENT RESULTS", "HIGHLIGHTS FROM THE QUARTER/YEAR", "Highlights from the report include:", "Highlights for the … are listed below:") and excludes the two CMG sub-headlines, Delta's terminated pointer sentence ("Highlights of the March quarter, … are on page five …" — terminator guard) and Airbnb's flattened-prose fragment ("highlights based suggested destinations …" — tail-word guard). The trailing-word branch is unchanged ("Selected Revenue Highlights", "Q1 2025 Financial Highlights (unaudited)"). Two coordinated changes were needed once the regex narrowed: (1) `_is_lede_heading_fragment` gains a carve-out — an all-caps line leading with "Highlights" that is NOT a highlights heading per the regex is a sub-headline, not a ≤4-word heading fragment (the Q3 fragment is 4 words; the real heading shapes "HIGHLIGHTS", "HIGHLIGHTS OF SEGMENT RESULTS", "HIGHLIGHTS FROM THE QUARTER" still drop); "RETURN" is deliberately NOT added to `_LEDE_HEADLINE_VERB_RE` — "Return on Equity" table labels would escape the table-header predicate. (2) The section collector splits the regex's two duties: `_HIGHLIGHTS_SECTION_ANCHOR_RE` keeps the broad pattern as the "a section starts here" signal (the CMG sub-headline anchored the section serving the dateline + bullets + quote + prose; Delta's pointer sentence anchored the quotes section — narrowing the anchor lost both, the first blast showed the CMG lede truncating at its 6-line budget and DAL flipping to the "Operations, Network and Fleet" section), and an anchor that is a leading-"Highlights" sub-headline (all-caps, unterminated, not a real heading) is prepended as the section's first content line — a terminated prose pointer stays a heading-only anchor. The 12-line section cap now counts FOLLOW lines only, so the prepended anchor cannot push the section's last line off (Chipotle's revenue prose); sections without a prepended anchor are byte-identical by construction.

## Batch 185 (2026-11-03): BRO orphaned flattened-table labels dropped; EOG supplement packet stays None; 5 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** Table mode for the lede loop, in four parts. (1) `_is_lede_flat_table_label` / `_is_lede_flat_table_label_shape`: a flattened table row's label (5–6 words, figure-less, unterminated) directly below a table header block (period header, table heading/header/title, units line, recon heading, bare period fragment) is skipped and enters table mode — Brown & Brown flattens recon tables one cell per line, so the label's `$-value` rows drop as a fragment run and the label is the only table line left; the old `_is_lede_table_label` (batch 160) could not see it because its next line is the next label, not a data row. The label-run prev branch was tried in v1 and removed: it mistook wrapped sub-headlines for label runs (AAPL/AXP). (2) `_is_lede_table_mode_residue`: inside table mode, an unterminated or colon-ended line is another table row (however long), a "Note:" line is a footnote even when terminated, a company-name line ending in a corporate suffix is residue (its period is an abbreviation), and a terminated line ending in "respectively." that carries a 4-digit year is a flattened multi-column row ("Treasury stock, at cost 20 shares at 2024, 20 shares at 2023, respectively."). Terminated prose and bullets still end the mode and are collected (CSX). (3) `_is_lede_nongaap_section_heading`: in table mode only, the bare heading "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" breaks the loop — the definitions prose under it is boilerplate. It sits at the top of the loop body because `_is_lede_title_line` (batch 178) also matches the bare heading and would skip it before a later break could run. (4) `table_seen` gate: prose reached in table mode with no content collected and no real table row seen since the mode started is filler after a TOC, not narrative after a table — the loop breaks instead of collecting it (batch 126: a TOC-only packet must stay None). A real table leaves data rows / unit lines / period headers behind, so a quote or paragraph after it is still collected; bullets are exempt. ## Batch 191 (2026-11-04): table-mode paragraph head served with its tail; AJG pretax paragraph whole; 6 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** new `_lede_wrapped_paragraph_head` + a residue-run tracker in the lede loop. AJG's pretax paragraph sits inside the summary-table region: its wrapped head lines are unterminated, so the loop skipped them as table-mode residue and only the terminated tail was served — a dangling fragment ("income taxes is shown on pages 14 and 15.") with no subject (batch 186's wrap-tail wart). When a terminated line is collected in table mode, the loop now scans the residue run back from its end (continuations are lowercase-led, a year wrap — "2024, the pretax impact ..." — is the one digit-led continuation allowed) to the first capital-led line, and prepends that suffix as the paragraph's head. Budget-neutral: only the tail counts against the 6-line budget, so the CEO quote after the paragraph keeps exactly the budget it had. The naive alternative (lowercase-led terminated lines as residue) would eat the CEO quote's own wrapped lines — this predicate only ever ADDS lines. A label can never be the head: the head must end mid-sentence (wrap tail per `_LEDE_WRAP_TAIL_RE`) while a label ends in "*" or ")" or a noun, and the scan passes over the orphaned table labels that precede the paragraph (the batch-185/186 label chains are in the same run — the first implementation required the whole run to be one paragraph and joined nothing; the suffix scan is what makes it work).

**Tests:** 5 in `tests/data/test_filings_batch191.py` (head shapes incl. year wrap and single-line head; negatives incl. orphaned-label pass-over, label-as-head, capital-led/short/terminated wraps, quote tail; 3 AJG real-exhibit end-to-end pins: Q3 2023, Q2 2024, Q4 2023). ## Batch 192 (2026-11-04): "#" and spaced-"*" footnote definitions are never highlights; APD's per-share "#" and non-GAAP "*" legends dropped; 1 stored row repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** two vocabulary changes in the shared footnote machinery, so every collection path (headline, lede, leading-bullet block, Highlights section) drops them. (1) `_FOOTNOTE_DEF_RE` gains a `^#\s*\S` shape: Air Products keys its per-share footnote "#" — "#Earnings per share is calculated ...", "#Per share amounts are calculated ...", "# Per share amounts are calculated ..." (attached and spaced forms across quarters) — and American Express its variance legend ("# - Denotes a variance of 100 percent or more."). Unlike "*", "#" never opens a bullet or prose in these exhibits (cache survey: only footnote definitions, legends, table fragments like DLR's "# of", and decorations "###" / "# # #"), so the spaced form is safe here where it is not for "*"; a bare "###" separator opens a block of length 1 (the next line is a heading, never a plausible wrap). (spaced, Q2 FY2026) and "*Certain results in this release, including in the highlights above, include references ..." (attached, Q1 FY2025) — was served as section content in Q2 FY2026 because the asterisk-note block is the one path that drops spaced-"*" notes and its lead list never covered this opener. The batch-165 "* Revenue grew 12 percent." bullet stays a bullet: the lead list stays note-shaped.

## Batch 194 (2026-11-05): "-more-" page markers end the highlights lede at the next section heading; truncated-tail repair exemption; 2 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `extract_press_release_highlights`):** the lede loop and the Highlights section collector never skipped the `-more-` page-continuation marker — the guidance collector gained the skip in batch 193, but the highlights paths did not, so APD Q2 FY2026 served `-more-` plus the next section's heading (`Fiscal 2026 Second Quarter Results by Business Segment`) as highlights. (1) `-more-` lines are skipped in both loops (never content, never budget — the lede loop previously swallowed them as table lines, the section collector as content). (2) A heading-shaped line right after a `-more-` ends the lede/section (`_is_more_page_section_heading`: ≤90 chars, unterminated, title-case, no $/%, not a bullet/dateline/all-caps line), when the previously collected line is terminated — the heading's content belongs to the next section. A paragraph wrapped across the page break is never heading-shaped (its head is sentence-case, or its previous line is unterminated), a quote-attribution tail ends with a comma or colon, and table mode suppresses the break (batch 185: prose after a table is still collected). ## Batch 195 (2026-11-05): bullet content gated by headings is served — leading-bullet intro skip + guidance-heading bullet look-ahead; 4 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `extract_press_release_highlights`):** APD Q1 FY2025 served only its headline + 1 dividend bullet (310 chars) although the release opens with its two top financial bullets and a Guidance bullet pair — two heading shapes gated the bullets. (1) The leading-bullet block broke on its first line, the colon-ended list intro `Q1 FY25 (comparisons versus prior year):` — the lede loop already skips such headings (batch 177) but the leading-bullet block never did, so the two financial bullets under it never competed. The block now skips a `_is_lede_colon_heading` line before any bullet is collected (same position as the dateline/period-header skips); when the line after the intro is not a bullet the else branch breaks the block exactly as before, so the skip alone can never create a block. (2) The Highlights section collector broke on the bare `Guidance` sub-heading via `_is_lede_table_heading` — the same predicate that ends a section at AppLovin's `First Quarter 2026 Financial Guidance Summary` table title. A guidance heading that introduces bullets is a sub-heading, not a table title, so the break now fires only when the next content line is not a bullet (`_next_content_line_is_bullet`: first non-admin line after the heading, `•`/`◦`/`·` count — a page-number admin line between heading and bullets does not hide them). The heading itself is collected as a label line (the stored APD row carries it as a non-defect line, and ADBE's served output already keeps section headings mid-section). The same look-ahead applies in the leading-bullet block's continuation branch. AppLovin's shape — guidance-summary heading followed by a table row — still breaks the section.
