## Batch 196 (2026-11-05): bare-word guidance headings with a footnote digit are headings (CI's OUTLOOK2 rescued); structural tail-drop repair for 194 stale stored guidance rows

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_is_guidance_heading`):** Cigna's outlook section is headed by the bare word with a superscript footnote digit (`OUTLOOK2` in text — the HTML is `OUTLOOK<sup>2</sup>`), so CI's 2024-12-31, 2025-03-31 and 2025-09-30 quarters extracted None while every other CI quarter (compound `2025 OUTLOOK2`, already accepted) served guidance. Batch 193's digit-strip path required a space in the stripped line (DAL's compound `Financial Guidance1` vs CRM's `Guidance5` table column header); the space requirement is dropped — the stripped line only has to match the heading regex. A census of the 1,699-exhibit cache finds exactly six bare-word+digit guidance headings: CI's three OUTLOOK2 (real section headings, followed by outlook prose + metrics table), CRM_2024-10-31's two Guidance5 (column headers inside the guidance section — the extractor already anchors on the earlier `Guidance` heading, so they can never become the anchor), and EMR_2025-09-30's `Guidance 2026` (also after the earlier `2026 Outlook` anchor). A bare-word+digit line can only anchor when no earlier guidance heading exists — i.e. when it IS the section heading, as in CI. The batch-193 test asserting the old rule is updated to the new behavior with a pointer to the batch-196 tests.

**Tests:** 9 in `tests/data/test_filings_batch196.py` (OUTLOOK2/Guidance5/compound-digit unit pins; CI ×3 live pins; CRM/EMR no-reanchor pins; APD two-bullets pin). Full suite: **1487 passed** (1478 + 9 new). `git diff --check` clean.

## Batch 198 (2026-11-05): line-leading bullet glyphs get a space after them in `_html_to_text` — glued `•Net sales` / `◦HOKA` / `▪Segment OI` bullets now render spaced on every served card; 215 stored guidance rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_html_to_text`):** inline formatting tags are stripped with no separator (deliberate — DFIN span-splitting, "RIS</span><span>K FACTORS"), so a bullet glyph in its own `<font>`/`<span>` glued to its item text (`&#8226;</font><font>Net sales...` → `•Net sales...`). The strip runs before the final `.strip()` — a leading space from a stripped opening tag otherwise hides the first line's bullet from the `^` anchor (caught by a unit pin). Mid-line bullets are untouched.

## Batch 199 (2026-11-05): First Solar guidance gaps — rule-line follower, intro-sentence anchors, wrapped figure lines, "N." footnote keys, dividend-declaration section ends; 63 stored guidance rows repaired + 20 NULL rows filled

**Fixes (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** five defects, one ticker's guidance section — plus the blast-wide fallout each fix carries.
1. **Rule-line follower:** `_is_guidance_section_end_follower` now skips rule-only lines (`^[-–—_=*]{3,}$`) when advancing to the real follower, like admin lines. First Solar's guidance table ends with a rule directly after its last row, and the rule matched the dash-led bullet branch, so `Volume Sold 15.6GW to 16.3GW` read as a next-section heading and the break dropped it (and the safe-harbor paragraph after the footnote block). Corrects the batch-198 carry-forward attribution: the drop was the follower test, not the collector's signal check — the signal check never fires on the row.
2. **Intro-sentence anchors:** a guidance-intro sentence now anchors the section (`_GUIDANCE_INTRO_RE`: `^our (updated|revised)? \d{4} guidance\b.*(as follows|summarized below)`). First Solar's interim releases introduce the table with prose ("Our 2024 guidance has been updated as follows:", "Our 2026 guidance remains unchanged and is summarized below:") and no heading, so 9 of 11 cached FSLR quarters extracted None despite carrying a full table. A census of the 1,699-exhibit cache finds this shape only in FSLR, and no serving exhibit has one before its real anchor.
3. **Wrapped figure lines:** the collector's all-caps break now requires a two-letter word, so a wrapped table value on its own line (`$520M` — FSLR's split "Operating Expenses" row) no longer breaks collection mid-table. A real heading ("CONFERENCE CALL DETAILS") always carries one.

Adjustment item resides in ...` — the batch-198 carry-forward shape, spaced form). The capital-after-number guard is unchanged, so decimal-led figures (`1.5 million shares ...`) still never open a block.
5. **Dividend declarations end the section:** `_is_guidance_next_section_heading` now returns True for a dividend-declaration heading (`Dividend Declaration`, `Quarterly Dividend`, `Dividend Payment`). Its follower paragraph carries "$0.48 per share", so the $-less follower test never fired on it and the declaration was collected as guidance (COR, EXPE, ADI ×12, EBAY ×3).

## Batch 200 (2026-11-05): guidance section-end misses — colon-ended headings, quote-led followers, results-table period-header followers; 31 stored guidance rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_is_guidance_next_section_heading` + `_is_guidance_section_end_follower`):** three defects, one defect class (the guidance section runs past its end into the next section).
1. **Colon-ended headings:** a trailing colon counted as sentence termination, so a colon-ended heading label never read as a next-section heading. `_is_guidance_next_section_heading` now treats a colon-ended line as unterminated for heading purposes (still gated on title case + the follower test, so a prose fragment like "We expect the following:" never qualifies). Cuts Cisco's "Editor's Notes:" + call-logistics bullets (×9 quarters), Disney's "Message From Our CEO:" + CEO quote (×7), GE's "Caution Concerning Forward Looking Statements:" + safe-harbor risk prose (×9). Guidance-word headings ("Q1 FY 2026 Guidance (1):", "Segment guidance is:") stay exempt via the vocabulary check, and period labels ("Fiscal Year 2027:") via the period-label check.
2. **Quote-led followers:** the follower test's `nxt[0].isupper()` failed on a quote-led paragraph (the opening curly quote is not a cased character), so a CEO quote after a heading never counted as a next-section follower. It now reads the first cased char. Bonus cut: Carnival's "Financing and Capital Activity" and "PROPEL: Powering Growth & Returns, Responsibly" headings (×2) — the PROPEL long-term-targets announcement no longer rides inside the FY2026 outlook.
3. **Colon + quotation follower:** Disney's Q2/Q3 FY2025 CEO quotes open with a wrapped fragment (no terminal punctuation on the first flattened line), so even the fixed follower test never fired. A colon-ended label followed by a quotation now ends the section outright — a speaker label, never guidance content. A non-colon heading + wrapped quote still does not end the section (pinned negative).
4. **Results-table period headers:** a period header ("Three months ended September 30", doubled "Three months ended ... Nine months ended ...") after a heading now counts as a section-end follower. Cuts GE Vernova's "Total Company Results" condensed-results-table tail (×11 quarters).

## Batch 203 (2026-11-06): section-tagline follower ends the guidance section; COIN "Product Update" cut, 1 stored row repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_is_guidance_section_end_follower`):** the batch-200 carry-forward (COIN "Product Update") is closed. "Product Update" is a real next-section heading, but its follower is a short tagline ("Building the future of finance, step by step" — 46 chars, unterminated) and the prose after it is wrapped, so its first flattened line is a fragment: neither the long-prose follower test (needs >= 60 chars, terminated, $-less) nor any other follower shape fired, and the heading was collected as guidance — the 30-line budget's last slot. A heading followed by a short sentence-case tagline and then a wrapped prose run that terminates within 6 lines and totals >= 100 chars now ends the section. A tagline is short (< 60), unterminated, carries no $/% (a figure line is a table row), is not a bullet/dateline/period header/quote, and is sentence-case, not title-case (a second heading/label is title-case: "Investor Relations", "CEO Comment", "BB+"). Two run guards keep the join from crossing a guidance table to a distant disclaimer paragraph: every non-terminating run line must be >= 50 chars (a wrapped prose line is near column width; a table row is short) and figure-sparse (at most one $/% character per 25 chars — GPC's "Global Automotive sales were $3.5 billion, up 0.8% ... with a 2.9% benefit ..." is 3 tokens in 110 chars; EL's "Forecasted/Adjusted EPS - Non-GAAP $3.10 - $3.35 $ 2.51 24% - 34%" is 4 in 68). ## Batch 205 (2026-11-06): results-boundary detector in the guidance main loop; DELL/ECL/DASH bleed cut, 17 stored guidance rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_GUIDANCE_RESULTS_PERIOD_RE` + `_is_results_table_ahead` + direct break in `extract_management_guidance`):** the batch-204 carry-forward (DELL/ECL/DASH guidance sections bleed into the reported results table) is closed. Two parts. (1) Generalize `_GUIDANCE_RESULTS_PERIOD_RE`: the old shape only matched the dated lowercase form ("Three months ended January 31"), so it missed the dateless/combined form ("Three Months Ended Fiscal Year Ended" — DELL; "Three Months Ended Y/Y % Change Q/Q % Change" — DASH), the quarter form ("First Quarter Ended March 31" — ECL) and the standalone fiscal-year form. A forward guidance period says "Ending", never "Ended", so the past tense is the discriminator — and as a follower it only fires after a heading candidate, which is how DELL/DASH now break at their results headings ("Fourth Quarter ... Financial Results", "Q3 2026 Financial Performance"). (2) A direct break in the main loop on the period header itself: ECL's two outlook bullets run straight into its results table with no heading line at all. The break needs guidance signal already delivered (a guidance table's own period header sits before any signal — AKAM's "Three Months Ended" intro) and a results-table confirmation ahead — a unit line ("(in millions, ...; unaudited)"), a standalone "Change"/"Reported"/"Adjusted" column label, or Y/Y-Q/Q change columns; a "Low End High End" range label anywhere in the 8-line window refuses (two passes, so a guidance table that prints a unit line first is still refused). ## Batch 206 (2026-11-06): page-footer furniture skip in the guidance collector; CCI tagline/domain lines cut, 8 stored guidance rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_BARE_DOMAIN_RE` + in-loop skips in `extract_management_guidance`):** the batch-205 carry-forward (CCI stored guidance rows carry "The pathway to possible." / "CrownCastle.com" furniture lines, 2 lines per occurrence, 11 occurrences across 8 stored rows) is closed. The "News Release continued" line was already skipped by `_ADMIN_LINE_RE` (its "news release" prefix); the tagline and the domain were not. A bare-domain line (a line that IS a domain, nothing else — no-spaces shape, so prose that merely mentions a domain never matches) is now skipped like an admin line, and a short (<= 60 chars) terminated sentence-case line immediately before a bare domain is skipped as the footer tagline. Investor Relations section") — when the notice sentence does not start the break line and the text before it ends with sentence punctuation, unterminated kept lines are popped so the text ends at the last complete sentence (the heading is never popped; runs only on a batch-209 notice match).

## Batch 210 (2026-11-07): table-of-contents anchor rejection in the guidance extractor; DLR over-collection closed; 8 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, `_is_toc_entry` + anchor-loop skip in `extract_management_guidance`):** the batch-209 carry-forward (DLR over-collection) is closed. Every DLR stored guidance row (8 quarters, ~748 chars each) was its financial supplement's table of contents: the extractor anchored on the contents-page entry for "2025 Outlook" (line 19 of the line stream, followed by the bare page number "10") and spent its whole line budget on TOC titles ("Consolidated Quarterly Statements of Operations", "Funds From Operations ...", ...). The real outlook section sits ~750 lines later ("Digital Realty raised its 2025 Core FFO per share outlook to $7.15 - $7.25 ...") and was never reached, because the function returns the first anchor whose collection clears 100 chars. A heading candidate is now a TOC entry when the next line is a bare page number AND the line after that is another title followed by another bare page number — two consecutive (title, page-number) pairs — and the anchor is skipped so scanning continues to the real heading. The two-pair requirement is the guard: a single bare number after a heading is often just a page footer — ELV's "Financial Guidance Summary" is followed by "6" and then "Elevance Health" (the next page's content), and SPG's "Guidance Reconciliation" by "43" and then "(1)" — neither is a contents page, and neither anchor may be skipped. Both shapes are pinned unchanged.

## Batch 215 (2026-11-08): AJG pretax-adjustment footnote note dropped from lede; CEO quote rescued; 6 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** AJG's summary-table footnote — "For fourth quarter 2023, the pretax impact of the Brokerage segment adjustments totals $559.5 million, ..." (three sentences: Brokerage / Risk Management / Corporate), the "*" footnote's definition of the adjustment items — sat between the summary table and the CEO quote, filling the 6-line lede budget and starving the quote (Q4 2023: the quote was lost entirely — the note is 5 lines against a budget already spent on the dateline and the CFO-Commentary pointer lines). The fix hooks the note into `_opens_footnote_def` via `_PRETAX_ADJUSTMENT_NOTE_RE` (exact shape: "For {first|second|third|fourth} quarter {YYYY}, the pretax impact of the {Brokerage|Risk Management|Corporate} segment adjustments totals $"), so the existing footnote-definition block skip consumes the note (wrapped continuations + chained segment sentences). Cache survey (1,699 exhibits): 11 opener lines, all AJG, all this exact shape. The full-year note ("For the year ended ...") and the nine/six-month period notes are deliberately NOT matched — they sit past the lede zone. Second half of the fix: the block skip clears table mode when the block opened with the pretax note — the note is prose that ends the summary-table region, and without the clear the quote's unterminated head lines were eaten as table-mode residue (the batch-191 head-prepend refuses quote heads), so the first blast lost the quote heads in 2024-06-30/09-30 and walked on to the nine-month note's tail in 2025-09-30. ## Batch 217 (2026-11-08): DAL 2024-12-31 wrapped narrative heading dropped from guidance; 1 stored row repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes batch 202's carried-forward item — DAL 2024-12-31 serves its results-narrative heading as two flattened lines, "Revenue Environment" / "and Outlook", so the single-line carve-out never fired and the stored guidance ended on the two heading fragments. New `_wrapped_guidance_narrative_end` joins a candidate with its next non-admin line and tests the joined form against the two narrative patterns (`_GUIDANCE_NARRATIVE_OUTLOOK_RE`, `_GUIDANCE_RESULTS_LED_RE`); `_is_guidance_next_section_heading` then tests the follower after the second fragment, and the collector breaks without appending either fragment. ## Batch 218 (2026-11-08): digit-only <sup> footnote keys spaced in the flattener; 33 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes batch 217's residual wart — `_html_to_text` stripped inline tags with no join, so a digit-only `<sup>` footnote key glued to its neighbors ("Financial Guidance1", "1Non-GAAP", "3Adjusted debt"; the older extractor spaced both sides). A digit key is never part of a split word (unlike DFIN span-split text), so the flattener now wraps digit keys in `\x02` markers before the inline-tag strip and resolves them to spaces at the end, once the neighbors are visible in flattened text. Space before the key unless it follows whitespace, a line start, "(" or "$"; space after it when a letter follows. Two guards: a bare key wedged between a digit and a letter stays glued on both sides (the "10²cm" shape — the one attested digit-letter case is parenthesized, "2025 (1) Sales"), and consecutive keys space apart ("word 1 2"). A run-length guard was considered and rejected: DE tables carry bare keys after 2-digit runs ("23 12", a footnote on a table value), so guarding on run length would corrupt them into "2312". Letter keys ("(a)", "th", "SM") and "®" are untouched — same class, separate batch. Census of the 1,699-exhibit cache: 4,097 digit-key sups; zero unit-exponent shapes ("m²", "ft²") and zero digit-key-digit chains, so a bare key after a digit is a footnote on a year/amount ("2022 3,"), never an exponent.

**Tests:** 9 in `tests/data/test_filings_batch218.py` (spacing units for word/key, line-leading key, year/amount keys, consecutive and multi-keys, and rejections for ordinals, letter keys, ®, the exponent wedge, span-split words and subscripts; real-exhibit pins DAL 2024-12-31 guidance 930 chars with "Financial Guidance 1" / "1 Non-GAAP" / "3 Adjusted debt", CI 2024-12-31 guidance still anchoring on "OUTLOOK 2", CI 2023-09-30 highlights with "operations 1,2"). 7 older pins updated to the spaced form (batch 193 DAL heading, batch 196 CI OUTLOOK ×3, batch 209 CI lengths 1143→1152 and 1108→1117, batch 217 DAL length 922→930 + "4 Introduced" tail); the `_is_guidance_heading` unit inputs stay glued — they test the anchor's digit-strip tolerance, which still accepts the old form. ## Batch 220 (2026-11-09): single-value key-metric lines rescued from the lede table-row filters; 23 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes the 4 drifted highlights rows batch 218 left open — and the drift class behind them. Citi's "2024 PAYOUT RATIO OF 58% (3)" was dropped from every quarter's highlights by two independent misclassifications: `_is_lede_data_row` counted the leading year ("2024") and the trailing footnote key ("(3)") as values, so 1 real value read as 3 figures in 6 tokens (50% density); and `_is_lede_table_line`'s footnote-tail branch caught any ≤6-word line ending in "(N)". The fix counts *value* figures — excluding a leading bare year and a trailing single-char paren key, the latter only when it occurs once and the line carries a % or $ value (a repeated "(2)" is a column value, not a footnote — the batch-159 "Acquisition and Disposition Impacts — (2) — (2)" pin, which the first cut of this fix broke and the refinement preserves). ## 2026-11-09 — Batch 222: highlights never end mid-sentence — completion allowance + clean-drop trim; 15 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes the finish-rule cutoff wart carried since batches 188/220/221. The lede finish rule's 4-line overrun cap (and the Highlights-section collector's 12-line cap, and the leading-bullet block's 14-line cap) stranded quotes/sentences mid-item, so stored highlights ended "“We have excellent" (AJG), "said David M. Cordani," (CI), "and slot" (GEV). Three parts, all gated on the finish rule's own unfinished signals: (1) completion allowance — when the cap is hit and the tail item is still unfinished (wrap tail, quote attribution, split attribution, tail quote open), allow up to 4 more lines (lede 4→8 past budget, section 12→16 follow lines, block 14→18) so the sentence can terminate and the quote close; (2) clean-drop trim (`_trim_unfinished_tail`) — when even the allowance is not enough (AJG's 12-line quotes, GEV Q3 2025's 5-lines-past-cap quote), drop the dangling tail back to the last complete sentence instead of serving the fragment (bullets, table residue and headings never touched; 200-char floor per batch 153); (3) the quote test is the TAIL test (`_lede_tail_quote_open` — the last quote event is an open) rather than the whole-text test, so a stray mark from an earlier quote cannot keep the allowance pulling after the tail's own quote closed; and the section collector judges qualification on a snapshot of its first 12 follow lines, so the extended tail's $/% figures can never flip a narrative section to "table".

**Probe (`scripts/batch222_probe.py`, `scripts/batch222_probe2.py`):** 2,491 stored highlights rows: 1,427 terminated, 428 bullet-tailed, 14 tableish, 46 genuinely mid-sentence (prose last line, wrap tail / open quote / comma), 576 other-unterminated (mostly headings). ## 2026-11-09 — Batch 223: numbered event announcements are narrative, not footnotes; all 8 drifted batch-222 repair skips resolved

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** `_is_bare_numbered_footnote` treated any terminated bare-numbered sentence as a footnote definition, so the Highlights-section collector dropped APLD's two "Recent Operational Highlights" items ("1.The Company announced on September 5, 2024 that it has entered into definitive agreements for a $160 million private placement financing ..." / "2.The Company added two additional clusters ..."). New exemption (`_BARE_NUMBERED_EVENT_RE`): a bare-numbered line opening "The Company" + an event verb (announced, added, launched, completed, entered into, signed, acquired, opened, appointed, expanded, introduced, received, began, closed, unveiled, named) is narrative, never a footnote — so it never opens a footnote-definition block on any path. The exemption is drawn on attested data, not guesswork: cache survey of all 4,034 bare-numbered footnote lines shows the "The Company / We" openers are otherwise definitions and disclaimers ("We define Adjusted Net Income ...", "The Company does not provide a reconciliation ...", "The Company declared and paid quarterly dividends ...", "We calculate average revenue per subscriber ..."), none of whose verbs is in the list; the two EL event-ish lines ("In fiscal 2025, the Company expanded ...", "From the end of August 2024 ..., the Company entered into agreements ...") do not start with the subject, so the anchored subject keeps them out; "declared" is deliberately NOT in the list (DKS's dividend footnote opens that way); a company-name subject ("American Express received the highest score ...", AXP's footnote-run item 6) is deliberately NOT exempted. A sequential-run exemption was surveyed and rejected: runs under Highlights headings are overwhelmingly footnote runs (AGNC's "1.Represents a non-GAAP measure. / 2.Please refer to ...", AXP's 6-item definition run, CCL's "1 See ... / 2 Fourth quarter record.") — APLD is the only genuine numbered list in the cache's Highlights zones.

## 2026-11-09 — Batch 224: the noun/number-ending hole — next-line lookahead + termination lookahead; 15 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes the finish-rule hole carried since batches 222/223. A cut landing on a line ending in a noun or figure ("Operating income was $746 million", "... related to the store portfolio") carries no unfinished signal, so the finish rule treated the item as complete and the trim could not see it either. Two parts, both gated on the sentence genuinely continuing: (1) lowercase lookahead (`_lede_next_line_continues(tail, nxt)`) — the next raw line starting lowercase means the sentence wraps on; wired into the lede finish-item decision and the completion allowance at all three caps (lede overrun 8, section 16, block 18). The tail must be unterminated: a terminated tail (a closed quote) followed by a lowercase-led line is a new sentence's wrap tail, not a continuation. (2) termination lookahead (`_lede_termination_ahead(collected, next_lines, limit=4)`) — the hard caps yield when the sentence terminates within the next 4 raw lines (Halliburton's sentence ends one line past the block's 18-line cap, "$748 million in the third quarter of 2025."), so the cap no longer strands it and the trim no longer walks it back further; the pull runs at most 4 lines past the cap, only while termination stays in sight. Gated on the sentence still being unfinished (or the next line continuing it): once the tail terminates, the pull stops even when another terminated line sits ahead.

**Probe (`scripts/batch224_probe.py`, `scripts/batch224_probe2.py`):** the 91 live-cut hole rows classify as 9 lowercase-continuation (ABNB, CI, DG ×4, HAL ×3 — the fixable class), 50 complete-item (complete bullets without terminal punctuation — false positives, left alone), 16 capital-continuation (new items/headings), 17 other (footnote markers, table residue), 178 no-cache. DAL 2024-09-30 is NOT a hole row after all: its tail is a complete bullet and the next line is the "Culture and People" section heading, so no continuation exists to pull; it has no stored row and serves live unchanged.

**Blast (guidance + highlights old-vs-new over 1,699 exhibits, `hidden_files/blast224/`):** **0 guidance diffs, 21 highlights diffs** — every one verified line-by-line. 19 terminate cleanly: the 9 target rows (HAL ×3, DG ×4, CI, ABNB 2024-09-30) plus DG 2024-05-03/2024-08-02, CI 2023-09-30, AJG 2024-12-31 (CEO thank-you quote completes), ETN 2023-12-31, GEV ×4 (CEO quotes complete), GPC 2026-09-30. ## 2026-11-10 — Batch 227: the wrap-fragment tail class — comma/semicolon/dangling-word cuts, truncate-at-terminator, colon-intro list labels, row-label qualifier strip; 29 stored rows repaired

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** closes the wrap-fragment tail class carried from batches 225/226. Four pieces wired into `_clean_highlights_result`'s trailing trim (the single final-assembly point): (1) `_is_trailing_wrap_fragment` — an unterminated prose tail ending mid-sentence: on a comma or semicolon, on a dangling function word ("of", "and", "to", "including", "the", "a" — Nasdaq's "Annualized Recurring Revenue (ARR)4 of", Goldman's "...during the second quarter of", Synopsys' "...at the midpoint, including"), with an open quote (Kroger's "“I joined Kroger because..."), or as a short lowercase noun phrase ("market share trends", General Mills — the sentence continues "improvement from fiscal 2024 levels." on the next source line); (2) `_truncate_trailing_fragment` — when the tail line's last terminated sentence is followed by an unfinished fragment, truncate the line at the terminator instead of dropping it (Coinbase's "...on that transition. Our customers trust us to store more crypto than any other company;" → "...on that transition."; Genuine Parts' "...comparable sales. Segment" → "...comparable sales."); (3) `_is_trailing_list_item_label` — a row label under a colon-ended list intro (Berkshire's "Other-than-temporary impairment of investments in Kraft Heinz and in Occidental" under "Net earnings includes:" — verbless, ≥8 words, figure-free, carries a statement-label noun; the batch-226 colon rule then pops the intro and the row-label predicate pops the line above, clearing the whole residue block); (4) a " - <qualifier>" strip in `_is_trailing_row_label` (BlackRock's "...attributable TO noncontrolling interests - Consolidated sponsored investment products" — a 1–6-word qualifier with no digits/$/% is stripped and the base re-tested). Guards throughout: bullets without terminal periods are the house style (AGNC's ◦ sub-bullets, AIG's ■ bullets, Palantir's ◦ bullets, WTW's "Adjusted Operating Margin was ...") and are never touched — a trailing value figure is the object of its "of" ("...ROE* of 11.7%"), so figures are never stripped before the dangle test; footnote markers ("...performance. 9", "...foreign exchange.*") are stripped before the terminated test; abbreviation dots ("Inc.", "U.S.", "ex.") are never split points; an imperative-led fragment ("See page 5 for details") and a figure-carrying one block the truncate; the short-lowercase branch requires the previous line to already end unfinished. The first blast caught two false positives: Cisco's "consecutive quarter" (a wrapped bullet completion — its previous line ends "fifth", so the gate keeps it) and Estee Lauder's "Affirms Fiscal 2027 Outlook ... 3% to 5%;" (a ";" separating headline items, not a sentence cut — a ";" after a headline verb is never a cut). The repair script's first cut had a loop-order bug (wrap-pop before truncate, so Kroger's comma tail was popped whole and the cascade stalled on the quote intro above it); fixed by mirroring the trim's order (residue → truncate → wrap-pop → colon). Repair review caught a bad truncate: Linde's "...ex. FX, growth" truncated to "...ex." — "ex" is now in the abbreviation list and the row is (correctly) skipped instead. The first-cut test run caught the verbless test missing ordinary verbs ("reduced"); `_TRAILING_COMMON_VERBS` (~30 finite verbs) makes the guard real.

## 2026-11-10 — Batch 230: the fragmented "· <word>" bullet openers — Dollar General's table-cell wrap orphans each bullet's first word; 8 stored rows repaired

**Probe (`scripts/batch230_probe.py`):** the carried-forward DG class from batch 229, scoped. The two stored DG rows (2026 Q1, 2026 Q2) read "· Net" / "Sales Increased 3.4% to $10.8 Billion" — the bullet's first word orphaned on its own line. Root cause is in the source HTML: each bullet is a table row whose text cell wraps after the first word ("Net\nSales Increased..."), and `_html_to_text` preserves the break. A full-cache survey found 94 exhibits with a marker + 1–2 word line, but only 10 carry the true shape (fragment + non-bullet continuation): DG ×8, ADSK ×1 ("· The" / "company has historically relied..."), DAL ×1 ("• Using" / "operating income..."). The rest are label lines ("• Same-restaurant sales:", "• Fiscal 2025:", "• Media: media@danaher.com" — all punctuated), sub-bullet headers ("• Revenues" heads a "◦" list; "• Other highlights:" heads "◦" items), or a bullet followed by another bullet (CCL "• Pricing", CTSH "• AI Services", DIS "▪ Higher attendance") — none of which may join.

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** new `_FRAGMENTED_BULLET_RE` (marker + one or two bare alphabetic words, no punctuation at all — a digit, figure, or punctuation mark means the line is already a complete item or a label) and `_join_fragmented_bullet_starts`, applied post-collection to the winning Highlights section, the lede list, and the guidance section's assembled lines — so qualification and the density competition see the unjoined lines exactly as before. The continuation must be a plain line: not another bullet (including a "◦" sub-bullet), not blank, not an all-caps heading, not a dateline, not admin/boilerplate, not a footnote-definition or table-units line. A bullet that wraps after a full clause is untouched — only the orphaned opener joins. The guidance path needed the same join: live verification caught the guidance card still serving the fragmented bullets ("· Net\n\nSales Increased...") on the same DG detail pages.

**Blast (guidance + highlights old-vs-new over 1,699 exhibits, `scripts/batch230_guidance_blast.py` / `scripts/batch230_cache_blast.py`, `hidden_files/blast230/`):** **7 guidance diffs, 2 highlights diffs**, all verified line-by-line. Guidance: DG 2024-08-02, 2024-11-01, 2025-01-31, 2025-05-02, 2025-08-01, 2026-05-01, 2026-07-31 — the guidance sections carry the same wrapped bullets, including "○ The" / "○ Diluted" sub-bullets in 2024-08-02 ("○ The Company now expects an immaterial impact to EPS...") and "· Share repurchases of up to $700 million" in 2026-07-31. No other ticker changes: the older DG quarters' highlights bullets lose the density competition to their prose sections, and the ADSK/DAL fragments sit in unserved text, so the join is a no-op for them.

(3) `_is_lede_data_row` counts a standalone "$" token as a figure for density (Fastenal's SG&A row reads 5/11 = 45% and is skipped as the data row it is); the shared `_LEDE_FIGURE_RE` is untouched.

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, +~500 lines):** new post-collection clean step `_clean_guidance_result`, hooked into `extract_management_guidance` just before the `"\n\n".join(...)` (collector untouched). It fuses split rows to `Label: v1 / v2`, or `Label: low – high` when the table's columns are exactly one Low/High pair and the row has exactly 2 figures in one value unit; merges dash-led value lines into the previous unit (`$3.2B` + `- $3.3B` = one range); drops footnote-definition blocks (shared opener via `_footnote_def_block_len` with an optional `opens` parameter, plus a guidance-local relaxed opener for glued keys like `2Includes...` and unterminated bare-numbered wraps like `3 We have not...` — only after a table value/fused row has been seen; drops only if the block terminates within 10 lines or runs to the end of collected lines); drops pure rule lines (`____...`); splits a units line carrying its Low/High headers. It keeps heading, units line, period sub-headings, prose, quotes; normalizes fused rows to `Label: values` when in table context. It refuses ambiguous shapes (leave as-is): wrapped labels (Emerson `Underlying Sales`/`Growth`, split ranges), 3+ value units, wordy values (`Greater than 10%`, `10% average` — Delta stays unfused), period sub-headings kept as section structure. A trailing qualifier moves off the label onto its values (`GAAP diluted EPS >` + `$5.94` → `GAAP diluted EPS: > $5.94`; `... share At least` → `... share: At least $37.20`; `... Up to` → `...: Up to $3.0 billion`; `... Step-up ---` → `... Step-up: --- $0.38` — a standalone dash token is the first column's missing-value marker); a bare month word is never a label (Elevance's `December 31,` date headers stay as-is); a label never opens with a qualifier and always carries an alphabetic word; a fused row's values must carry a real figure (bare `(N)` keys and bare 4-digit years filtered). `_footnote_def_block_len` gained an optional `opens` parameter (default `_opens_footnote_def`); highlights/lede behavior byte-identical.

## 2026-11-13 — Batch 246: the executive quote after the dateline is served — 85 stored highlights rows re-synced; SKIP-loss 202→189

**Probe (`scripts/batch246_probe.py`, `scripts/batch246_probe2.py`, `scripts/batch246_probe3.py`):** the batch-245 design question, answered with a blast. The strict quote classifier (quote-first or attribution-first, quote opens within 140 chars and closes; Ford's flattened mega-line with a buried `“adjusted”` excluded) finds 44 loss rows carrying quotes, 20 of them quote-only. The mechanism is the leading-bullet block: the dateline sentence closes the bullet item and the block breaks before the quote (ADI/DECK/ADSK). But the seed rows are split — ADI/DECK/DGX carry the quote, Broadcom/Dollar Tree/Elevance/GD do not — so stored cannot settle whether quotes belong in highlights; the decision is a product one, and the blast sizes it: 85 rows change, every added line a genuine executive quote, 0 rows lose content.

**Fix (extractor, `src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** `_leading_bullet_block` pulls the quote run — consecutive `_is_executive_quote_line` lines, at most 3 — that immediately follows the dateline closing the bullet item, then ends the block (the results table follows). The dateline test is local to the pull-in (`_is_quote_pull_dateline`): the shared dateline regexes miss the glued-dash (`WILMINGTON, Mass.--November 26, 2024--`), all-caps-month (`SAN FRANCISCO, MAY 22, 2025--`), parenthesized-date (`Goleta, California (October 24, 2024) --`), and two-comma (`SECAUCUS, N.J., October 22, 2024 -`) forms, and widening the shared regexes would be wrong — the block breaks on a dated dateline mid-block, so a matching dateline would drop out of the block instead of riding in as a continuation. The two-comma form alone widens the blast from 48 to 85 rows (ABBV ×8, CARR ×5, CTSH ×6, FIS ×7 join). Full-cache blast: 72 B→S4 + 13 SKIP-loss→S4, 0 other diffs; probe3 verifies 83/85 rows quote-only (the 2 DGX exceptions are the headline-join artifact — stored splits the headline across 2 lines, live joins it — which gate S4's headline alignment already handles).

**Repair:** the 85 S4 rows re-synced with the existing gate-S4 repair (`scripts/batch242_repair.py`): 89 quote lines added in total (ADI ×8, AVGO ×8, DECK ×8, DLTR ×7, ELV ×8, GD ×7, ABBV ×8, FIS ×7, CTSH ×6, CARR ×5, DGX ×5, D ×1, EQIX ×1, AEP ×1, AMAT ×1, CI ×1, CVS ×2, DD ×1). Post-repair census: B 1001 (was 988), SKIP-loss 189, S4 0 — the repair is idempotent (dry re-run finds 0 S4 rows). The S4 gate's one-directional loss check is what blesses the swap: no stored line is lost, no table is added, and the added lines are doc-verified quotes. Side effects folded into the re-sync: 9 ADI/DECK rows change joining from `\n\n` to `\n` (renders the same under `whitespace-pre-line`) and ADI 2024-11-02's truncated stored dateline (`...which end`) is completed to the full sentence.

## 2026-11-13 — Batch 247: the doc-aware trailing-furniture gate S6 — ADSK ×6 re-synced; SKIP-loss 189→183

**Probe (`scripts/batch247_probe.py`, `scripts/batch247_probe2.py`):** the batch-246 carry-forward, decomposed exactly. All six ADSK loss rows differ from live in the same two ways only: the stored dateline reads `SAN FRANCISCO, MAY 22, 2025 -- Autodesk ...` vs live `2025-- Autodesk` (spacing-only), and the stored row ends on a trailing table-furniture run — a bare period label (`First Quarter Fiscal 2026`) plus, on five of the six, the results-table units header (`(In millions, except percentages and per share amounts) Q1 FY26 YoY Change`). ## 2026-11-14 — Batch 252: sub-headline guard for the ≤4-word fragment rule + %-range guidance statements — 7 stored highlights rows re-synced; SKIP-loss 165→162

**Probe (`scripts/batch252_probe.py`):** the batch-251 carry-forward, re-censused with the full gate chain (in-sync 1032, SKIP-loss 165, live-none 2, nocache 1326). The three blocked CHD rows decompose into two extractor defects, both now attributed. (1) The ≤4-word `_is_lede_heading_fragment` branch eats short sub-headlines unconditionally: "ANNOUNCES 4% DIVIDEND INCREASE" (4 words, verb ANNOUNCES, 4%) and "TOUCHLAND ACQUISITION COMPLETED" (3 words) are dropped even though the 5–8-word band already spares verb/figure-carrying lines. (2) The 2026-OUTLOOK line ("2026 OUTLOOK OF ORGANIC SALES GROWTH OF 3-4% and ADJUSTED EPS GROWTH OF 5-8%") is dropped by `_is_lede_data_row`'s 25% branch — `_LEDE_FIGURE_RE` counts each hyphenated %-range as two figures ("3", "4%"), so the line reads 4 figures over 14 tokens and ends in a figure. The first fix attempt (verb guard at ≤4 words) regressed the blast: AWK ×2 and CHD 2025-03-31 went in-sync → loss/s4 ("AFFIRMS LONG-TERM TARGETS", "Q1 EPS EXCEEDS OUTLOOK", "UPDATES FULL YEAR OUTLOOK" are 4-word verb lines that read as headings, and sparing them starves a real bullet under the 6-line budget), EIX ×8 went to loss (a bullet-led %-range line, "● Reiterates ... 5%-7% ...", was served budget-free, letting the dateline paragraph in), and FAST went to loss (a negative value's minus, "2.02 -0.6 %", read as a range dash, so two table rows rode the lede). All three misfires are fixed in the shipped version (see Fix).

**Fix (extractor, `src/tickerlens/data/filings.py` — no new gate):** (a) `_is_lede_heading_fragment`: the ≤4-word branch now spares a line carrying a $/% figure, or — at ≤3 words — a completed-event statement (`COMPLETED`, added to `_LEDE_HEADLINE_VERB_RE` for the 5–8-word band too). A present-tense verb at ≤3–4 words does not distinguish a sub-headline from a section heading, while a completed-event statement is news by construction — a heading names a topic, it never states that an event is complete. (b) New `_is_lede_percent_range_statement` + `_LEDE_PERCENT_RANGE_RE`: a %-to-% range carried by ≥4 alphabetic words is a guidance statement, exempt from `_is_lede_data_row` (the %-range mirror of the batch-183 $-range exemption) and served budget-free in the lede loop like the $-range statement. The range connector is "to", a spaced dash, or a hyphen/dash between two digits (or a % and a digit, "5%-7%") — never the minus of a negative value; a bullet is never a range statement. A bare range fragment ("3% to 4%") and a short %-range table row ("Net Sales Growth (0.5%) - 0.5% 1.5% - 3.5%", 3-word label) stay data rows. Post-fix blast: exactly the three CHD rows move loss → S9, four rows move in-sync → S4 (BBY, DKS, DUK, EL — each gains a real guidance line and loses nothing), and no row moves to loss.

**Repair (`scripts/batch252_repair.py`, full gate chain re-run, no new gate):** 7 rows re-synced — CHD 2024-12-31, 2025-06-30, 2025-12-31 via S9 (only the two summary-table headings lost, tail bullets added), BBY 2026-08-01, DKS 2026-08-01, DUK 2025-12-31, EL 2026-06-30 via S4 (each a pure guidance-line addition: BBY "Raises FY27 Comparable Sales Guidance to 1.9% to 3.0%", DKS the two "○ ... comparable sales outlook ..." bullets, DUK "introducing 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.55 to $6.80 ... 5% to 7% through 2030", EL "Raises Outlook on Adjusted Operating Margin to 12.7% to 13.5%" plus the dateline paragraph). **Probe (`scripts/batch253_probe.py`):** re-census with the full gate chain (in-sync 1035, SKIP-loss 162, live-none 2, nocache 1326). The DLR ×7 cohort decomposes into one extractor defect with a three-link failure chain. (1) DLR's exhibits are combined release+supplement packets: the doc opens with the supplement's TOC ("Table of Contents" / "Financial Supplement" / section titles + page numbers), and the real release headline ("Digital Realty Reports First Quarter 2026 Results") sits ~530 lines in, ahead of a "Highlights" bullet section. (2) `_skip_toc` never fires on the first TOC heading: the very next line, "Exhibit 99.1", matches `_ADMIN_LINE_RE`, and the scan loop breaks on any admin line before collecting a page number (pages=0 < 2), so the headline pass picks "Table of Contents" and the lede's 6-line budget fills with TOC entries. (3) The section path — which is what produced the good stored rows — fails for a different reason: the "Highlights" section is rejected by `_looks_like_financial_table`. DLR's bullets use the black-square marker "◾" (U+25FE), which is not in `_BULLET_LEAD_RE`, so two $+%-carrying ◾ bullets count as data rows and, with the two $+%-carrying "Financial Results" narrative lines, trip the data_rows >= 4 threshold. The batch-154 defect class, a new glyph. The `_skip_toc` direction was tried first and rejected: a monkeypatched skip that consumes the exhibit-label line lands the headline pass in the supplement's "Corporate Profile" prose and the whole extraction returns None — the section path is the right fix, because the stored rows prove it produces the right output once the section qualifies.

**Fix (extractor, `src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** "◾" joins `_BULLET_LEAD_RE`'s glyph class (no space required, like the batch-154 glyphs). ## 2026-11-15 — Batch 258: DLR "Table of Contents" headline wart fixed — 8 stored rows re-synced with real headlines; census unchanged (in-sync 1059, SKIP-loss 142)

**Probe (`scripts/batch258_probe.py`):** all 8 stored DLR rows carried the literal headline "Table of Contents" (live and stored agreed, so the census counted them in-sync — the wart was invisible to the gate chain). The mechanism, traced on DLR 2025-06-30: the packet opens `EX-99.1 / 2 / dlr-...htm / EX-99.1 / Table of Contents / Exhibit 99.1 / Table of Contents / Financial Supplement / ...` with a page-numbered TOC through page 33, then supplement front matter (corporate profile, management, analyst coverage, key-data tables), a second TOC, and the real headline at line 596 ("Digital Realty Reports Second Quarter 2025 Results"). `_skip_toc` never ran: its admin-break fired at once on the "Exhibit 99.1" line (batch-110's `^exhibit[\s\-]+99(\.1)?\b` admin branch), breaking the scan with pages=0, so the headline loop fell through and picked "Table of Contents" as the headline.

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, 3 parts):** (1) `_skip_toc` consumes an exhibit-marker line (`_TOC_EXHIBIT_MARKER_RE`: "Exhibit 99.1" / "EXHIBIT-99.1" / the "ECHIBIT" typo / ticker-prefixed) as TOC material instead of breaking — the marker is packet front-matter, not a narrative marker; contacts, release banners and date lines still break the scan. The skip then lands past the TOC (line 72, the corporate-profile paragraph). (2) An `after_toc` guarded scan in the headline loop: after a TOC skip, long lines are skipped instead of breaking with headline=None, and only a headline-shaped line with a headline verb + results topic (`_NARRATIVE_TAIL_RE`) is picked — the supplement's headline-shaped decoys ("Key Quarterly Financial Data", the "Unaudited, Dollars ..." units line, section labels, addresses, tables) are all passed over. The single-word-fragment join ("DLR" + "Series J Preferred Stock:") gets the same verb+topic requirement in the after-TOC state — it was the first decoy the scan landed on. (3) The dateline branch skips instead of breaking in the after-TOC state: EOG's supplement-only packet (tables all the way down, honestly None) has a table row that trips the city-dateline shape ("Acquisition Costs of Other Property, Plant and Equipment (134) —"), and the unguarded scan broke there with body_start past the row, serving the "Net Debt-to-Total Capitalization Ratio" section as the lede. With the guard the scan runs to end-of-doc and EOG stays None, as before.

**Blast (`scripts/batch258_blast.py`, 1699 cached exhibits):** exactly 12 rows move, all DLR, all improvements — 11 stored quarters from "Table of Contents" to their real "Digital Realty Reports ... Results" headline (bodies byte-identical), plus DLR 2023-12-31 from None to its real headline + 802 chars (pre-window cached quarter, no stored row). EOG ×3 and all 1684 other exhibits byte-identical. One test in the suite pinned the wart (`test_filings_batch225.py::test_dlr_toc_only_result_unchanged_by_floor`, which documented the wart as a known separate item) — updated to the real headline, since this batch is that fix.

**Repair (`scripts/batch258_repair.py`, strict by construction):** a row updates only when its stored first line is exactly "Table of Contents", live extraction from its cached exhibit succeeds, and the stored body (after the first line) is byte-identical to the live body. 8/8 rows re-synced (2024-06-30 through 2026-03-31); dry re-run finds 0 rows with the wart (idempotent). Post-repair census: B 1059, SKIP-loss 142, live-none 2, nocache 1328 — unchanged, since the DLR rows were in-sync before (wart in both) and stay in-sync (real headline in both).

**Probe (`scripts/batch259_probe.py`, `scripts/batch259_trace.py`):** the carried-forward CHD item, traced on CHD 2024-03-31: the release opens with the headline, two caps sub-headlines ("Q1 NET SALES, GROSS MARGIN AND EPS EXCEED OUTLOOK", "RAISES OUTLOOK FOR FULL YEAR GROSS MARGIN AND EPS"), two section labels ("2024 First Quarter Results", "2024 Full Year Outlook"), then 5 Q1 bullets + 5 FY-outlook bullets. The 2025-03-31 release, with no sub-headlines, served 6.

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`, lede loop):** a bullet run is a sequence of discrete items, not a prose paragraph: while the next line is a bullet and the last collected line is one too, collection continues past the 6-line budget up to the 12-line section cap. A non-bullet past the budget still falls through to the finish logic, so prose ledes keep the hard 6-line cap and the run can never pull in the dateline or the CEO quote. Two guards found by the blast: (1) a colon-ended bullet is a sub-list opener, not a complete item ("• For the nine months ended March 31, 2025:", "• ... Expand Profit Recovery and Growth Plan to:") — its items sit on ◦ lines the loop does not recognize as bullets, so collecting the opener strands the lede at an unfinished item and the overrun path then pulls the sub-list plus the next section heading (EL 2025-03-31 served "BEAUTY GAINS AND OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS3" as a highlight; the mechanism is the unbalanced CEO quote — the nested "Beauty Reimagined" quote leaves `_lede_quote_is_open` true, which suppresses the sentence-terminated break — and ABT/EL Q4 served the opener dangling with nothing after it). The opener is refused, so the bullet-break ends the lede cleanly instead. (2) Bullets directly after the headline take the leading-bullet-block path (18-line cap), not the lede — the extension only fires inside a run the lede already collected.

## 2026-11-16 — Batch 263: the colon-opener sub-list is served — lede lookahead + leading-block bullet-run extension + overrun caps-heading guard; 41 stored rows re-synced; tail 1→0

**Probe (`scripts/batch263_probe.py`, `scripts/batch263_probe2.py`, `scripts/batch263_probe3.py`):** the batch-262 carry-forward splits into two paths, not one. DIS_2025-09-27 is a *leading-bullet-block* case, not a lede case (no LEDE_DEBUG trace): the block hits its 14-line cap exactly on the "• Sports: … For Q4:" parent, and the completion allowance refuses because a colon-ended parent is not "unfinished" by the finish rule's signals (its continuation is a bullet, not a prose continuation) — so the Sports ◦ children + Experiences parent + children strand. EL_2025-03-31 is the lede case: the opener sits at content 8 with its three ◦ children directly after it, then a "Page 2 of 20" admin line, then the "BEAUTY GAINS AND OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS3" heading. ABT_2025-12-31's opener sits at content 11 with two • children after it.

**Fix (`src/tickerlens/data/filings.py`):** three changes, one mechanism (batch 262 made the batch-259 premise — ◦ items unrecognized as bullets — false). (1) Lede extension: a colon-ended bullet is collected exactly when its items are bullets — the next content line is a bullet start (`_next_content_line_is_bullet`) — and there is room for at least one child (content < 11); a table-intro opener (Berkshire's "Net earnings includes:") is still refused because its continuation is table rows, not bullets. (2) Leading-block cap: the batch-259 bullet-run extension mirrored — while the next content line is a bullet and the last collected line is one too, collection continues to the 18-line bound the completion allowance already trusts; a mid-block heading still ends the block because it is appended as a continuation and is then the last collected line, not a bullet start. (3) Overrun caps-heading guard (`_is_lede_caps_heading`): the overrun path never pulls a section heading as a "continuation" — the heading ends the lede instead. A repeated page header inside a wrapped item is the exception: the line after the header is checked with the batch-224 `_lede_next_line_continues` signal, and when it continues the item the header is skipped transparently so the continuation is pulled without the header riding mid-bullet.

## 2026-11-16 — Passcode gate for the public site (user request)

**What:** the live Railway site had no auth — anyone with the link could use it. Added a shared-passcode gate: new `src/tickerlens/auth.py` (HMAC-signed cookie, 30-day remember; `Authorization: Bearer <passcode>` also accepted for the future iOS client), `GET/POST /login` + `GET /logout` + `GET /healthz` (exempt liveness probe), `PasscodeGateMiddleware` (redirects unauthenticated visitors to `/login?next=…`, open-redirect-guarded), and a standalone `templates/login.html` in the app's design language (TL mark, indigo Continue, dark-mode aware — no nav, no HTMX). The gate is active only when `TICKERLENS_PASSCODE` is set (new optional `Settings` field); unset = open (local dev unchanged, startup logs a warning). `python-multipart` added to pyproject + requirements.txt (form parsing) — it must be present in BOTH the `.venv` (tests) and the system python's user site-packages (the dev server runs under system `python3`, not the venv; see AGENTS.md).

**Tests:** `tests/test_passcode_gate.py` — 17 tests (gate off: home 200, /login bounces home; gate on: unauth → 307 to /login, login form renders, wrong passcode 401, correct 303 + HttpOnly cookie, safe `next` honoured / off-site `next` sanitised to /, cookie unlocks pages, Bearer unlocks / wrong Bearer stays locked, logout re-locks, /healthz + /static exempt). Full suite **2379 passed** (2362 + 17). `git diff --check` clean.

**Live verification:** gated dev server on :8123 — unauth home 307 → /login, /login 200 with the form, /healthz 200; wrong passcode 401; correct passcode 303 + `tickerlens_auth` cookie; home + /company/AAPL 200 with the cookie. Styled screenshot `~/workspace/tickerlens-shots/login.png` verified (clean centered card, light mode). Screenshot gate satisfied.

**Status:** committed locally; **not pushed** — the gate ships inert until `TICKERLENS_PASSCODE` is set in Railway. Sequence once the user picks the passcode: set the env var in Railway first, then push (Railway auto-deploys on push to main — verified 2026-11-16 ~22:14 CST: auto-deploy ON, live deployment is 7599bc7, no watch paths / healthcheck / Wait-for-CI gating anything). The passcode value itself is never stored in the repo or in chat memory.

**Not fixed (carried forward):** the live site's database does NOT refresh on push — the entrypoint seeds `/data/tickerlens.db` from the image only on first boot, and batches don't commit the DB, so batch data fixes (e.g. BKR in batch 267) won't appear on the live site until a DB sync is wired. Code deploys automatically; data does not yet. Known limits of the gate itself: no brute-force throttling, no CSRF token on the login form (a login CSRF can only log the victim in) — acceptable for a friends-shared link, revisit if the link goes wider.

One bug caught by the V probe before commit: the first form appended the continued heading label twice (once at the heading break, once in the continuation branch) — fixed with a `continue` after the append (the cap check is skipped for the label line only; the bullet the gate just confirmed follows immediately and runs it).

## 2026-11-18 — Batch 275: norm() cross-line glue fixed — footnote-key rule moves per-line; DASH_2025-06-30 re-synced, census B 1126 / SKIP-loss 80

**Diagnosis (`scripts/batch275_probe.py`):** the defect batch 274 deferred: `norm()` in `scripts/batch231_repair.py` claimed to be per-line ("literal spaces, never \s, so a rule can never join two lines") but its footnote-key rule `([,.])\s+(\d)` ran on the whole string, and `\s` matches a newline — so a line ending in "." or "," glued to a digit-starting next line. Probe over all 2,543 stored rows + live extractions: 31 stored rows and 7 live extractions carried glued lines (AFRM, CSX, DASH, every F lede + segment pair — the F lede 2910 chars + segment 2256 chars fused into one 5162-char normed line). The same-class trademark rule `\s+([®™©])` was checked and left alone: zero lines starting with ®/™/© in any live extraction, so it has no attested cross-line case.

**Fix (`scripts/batch231_repair.py`):** the footnote-key rule moves from the whole-string block into the per-line loop, as `([,.])[ \t]+(\d)(?=[ \t]|$)` placed right after the space-before-comma/period rule (order-insensitive with it: "word , 1" reaches "word,1" either way). Literal spaces/tabs only, so a rule can never join two lines again. No `src/` change — `norm()` lives in the audit/repair tooling, so live serving is untouched; the fix corrects what the census and gates compare. Post-fix probe: glued rows 31+7 → 0.

**Census + repair:** old-norm census re-run for a clean baseline (via a temporary stash): B 1125 / SKIP-loss 81, DASH ×4. Post-repair census: **B 1126, SKIP-loss 80** — DASH ×3 remaining. No other row moves anywhere in the 2,543-row census.
